short: Build a living ant colony that can stay on your desktop while you work. Hatch unusual ants, place nest and food rooms, collect coins, and expand from a glass habitat into drawers, pipes, walls, roots, and the forgotten depths below.
about: Start with five tiny ants in a glass habitat. Hatch new workers, build their home, and watch every trip for food turn into coins—then leave them working quietly while you do something else.   ANT is a hand-drawn idle colony simulator and desktop companion. Keep a slim colony along the edge of your screen, or open the full colony and follow your ants as their tiny home spreads far beyond the glass.   A Living Colony on Your Desktop🐜   Pin ANT to your screen, choose a compact size, and let the colony keep moving while you work, watch videos, browse, or play something else. The ants collect food and earn coins automatically without demanding constant attention. When you are ready to build, open the full colony with one click.           Every Ant Begins as an Egg🥚   Buy an ant and watch its small white egg hatch before the new worker joins the trails. Discover more than 40 ant types with distinct colors, silhouettes, animations, income values, and visual gimmicks—from workers, leafcutters, and honeypot ants to ghost, robot, fossil, cosmic, and far stranger varieties.   Build Space for a Growing Swarm🪴   Your colony needs more than numbers. Buy and place nest rooms to increase capacity, add food rooms that ants can visit, and choose between increasingly large room sizes as the population grows. Ants distribute themselves across available rooms instead of crowding into a single chamber.   Dig Through a Hidden World🪏   The glass habitat is only the beginning. Excavate the cabinet one section at a time, then continue through pipes, wall cavities, garden soil, tangled roots, clay, stone, underground water, and forgotten layers far below the house. Each expansion reveals new building space, routes, scenery, and discoveries.           Turn Tiny Clicks into Enormous Numbers🖱️   Click the surface food for an early boost, upgrade your click power, and reinvest every coin into stronger ants and a larger home. Find an occasional sugar cube to trigger a 60-second Sugar Rush that doubles your income. Your colony also earns part of its income for up to eight hours while you are away. name: Cutie Office
lang: English, Korean
short: What if your PC were a tiny pixel company? Every CPU core types away at a desk, every program you open clocks in for work, and the office cat naps when things are quiet. A cozy desktop companion that turns your computer's real activity into a living office.
about: Cutie Office turns your PC into a tiny pixel company, live.   Every CPU core is an employee typing at a desk. Every program you open walks in through the front door. Your memory fills the archive, your graphics card paints in the design studio, and when your computer goes quiet, the office cat curls up for a nap.  It isn't a simulation of a computer. It  is  your computer, just much cuter.                CPU → Compute Dept.  One employee per core. The busier the core, the faster they type, until they sweat and steam. Idle cores nap on their keyboards.    Programs → Staff.  Launch an app and it clocks in; close it and it heads home. Busy apps work at the meeting table; idle ones relax on the sofa, play ping-pong or grab a coffee.    Memory → Rank.  The more memory a program uses, the higher it climbs, from Intern all the way to Director.    Your active window  presents to the boss at the whiteboard.            RAM  fills the archive shelves with binders.    GPU  designers paint as hard as your graphics card works, and nap when a discrete GPU goes to sleep.    Disks  are a busy warehouse with a forklift, and  network  traffic is a flurry of envelopes in the mail room.    Battery  is the pantry coffee pot. Plug in the charger and it starts brewing.    Sound : every speaker, headset and audio interface gets its own unit in the lounge sound rack, and the woofer thumps whenever something plays.    Data on the move : boxes come up from the warehouse through the archive's service window, a clerk carries folders to the busy desks, and capsules whoosh through a pneumatic tube to the design studio. When memory fills up, the overflow is stored away in the warehouse.              Minimize Cutie Office and a tiny office docks at the bottom of your screen, so your staff keep working right on your desktop while you do. Want it bigger? Mini mode and Always-on-top have you covered. Close the window and the office keeps running in the system tray, or quits completely: you decide. In the dock your staff share little moments too: high fives, light-bulb ideas, coffee breaks and parcels landing right in their hands.      Poke an employee and they jump in surprise. Keep poking and they grumble, get angry, and finally storm off to sulk. Pick them up and toss them across the office: they bounce, get dizzy and wander back to their desk. It works in the mini dock too, and HR is keeping count…      Switch on the desktop buddy (Settings → Window) and the employee of the program you're using comes out on top of its window. They perch on the title bar, ride along when you drag the window, and nap when things are quiet. You can pick them up and throw them, too. Clicks go straight through to your window, they hide in full screen, and any employee can be sent back to the office with one click.        A live view of your real PC: CPU, memory, GPU, disks, network, audio devices, battery and temperature   Made for every PC, from thin laptops to 128-thread workstations with drives from C: to Z:, several GPUs and racks of audio interfaces   Every program keeps a work record and levels up its career; colleagues cheer when someone levels up, and staff who work too long get tired and head for coffee   Your staff earn performance points as they work: spend them on 10 decorations (aquarium, cat tower, arcade, gallery, golden lucky cat…)   A daily work report with the MVP of the day, and the employee of the week framed in the CEO's office   Click any employee or room for a detail card with live graphs   A sky and lighting that follow your real time of day   Cute, quiet sound effects, a pixel-art cursor and bouncy buttons, with optional office-life sounds (typing, coffee sips, yawns)   A work log of every clock-in, clock-out and office incident   39 Steam Achievements, all earnable on any PC just by using it: quick wins for day one, and long-haul goals for the dedicated   Name your own company and CEO   Streamer mode hides window titles and your PC's name   English

name: His Big Bull
lang: Simplified Chinese, English, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Japanese, Korean
short: A little bull for your Windows desktop. Pick from 24 characters, feed him, watch him nap, or take a break with fishing, mahjong and mini-games. Keep notes and clipboard history nearby, and turn your own photos into animated desktop companions.
about: Make room for a little bull His Big Bull is a pet for your Windows desktop. He wanders, grazes and naps, responds when you pet him, and reacts to some of the apps you use. Give him a snack or a pat. When you need to concentrate, let him stay quiet. Choose from 24 characters with different looks, animations and activities. Want another little companion? Drag a bull from the character picker onto an empty spot on your desktop. Toss your desktop icons around Grab physics copies of your current desktop icons, fling them around and watch them collide and bounce. This desktop interaction is separate from Icon Pushing below. It does not delete or relocate your real files. Something to play during a break The Games menu brings together eight activities: Bull Baseball Build a bat from copies of desktop icons, swing it with the mouse and knock the bull towards a target. Icon Pushing Pick a desktop icon and let your bull push it in the direction you choose, with an undo option. This changes the real icon’s desktop position, without deleting or relocating the file. Zombie Horde Fight zombies and bosses, then fling icon copies at enemies with Desktop Power. Bull Cards Play mahjong, Dou Dizhu, Make 24, blackjack (21), Texas Hold’em and bluffing cards with bull opponents. Make 24 is an arithmetic puzzle: combine four numbers with addition, subtraction, multiplication and division to reach 24. It is a separate game from blackjack. Bull Tycoon Roll dice, buy land, build houses and develop your properties. Pasture & Fishing Mark out a patch of desktop for a pasture or pond, go fishing, hunt for treasures and clean up relics.  You can also prepare your catch: scrape off the scales, clean up the fish, then sell it.         Keep your catch in a desktop aquarium Fish you catch can be cleaned and sold, or kept in a separate desktop aquarium. Feed them, watch them swim, choose a tank and upgrade its capacity as your collection grows. Angry Bull Pull back a slingshot, aim and work through the levels. Bull Racing Drive along Task Manager's CPU graph. A and D control driving and rotation in the air.         A few useful things within reach Browse your clipboard history, edit and save screenshots, set a timer or jot down a note. Workspaces remember apps, folders and windows so you can reopen them later; they cannot recover unsaved document contents. You can also make QR codes or listen to ambient sounds. Photo cutouts let you make a 2D desktop character from your own picture. Adjust its bones, try a walking animation, or turn on ragdoll physics and drag it around with the mouse. Some characters also offer planning lists, translation and song recognition through their character menus. A note now, a nudge later Keep a simple memo, or add a date and time. Your bull can call and show the note in a speech bubble when it is due; open longer notes to read them in full. Planner Bull keeps task lists and progress separate from these quick notes. Reminders need the app to be running. Missed reminders can appear after you reopen it, when interruptions are allowed. You can also layer ambient sounds to make your own background mix. Before you start For Windows 10/11 64-bit, using a mouse and keyboard. CPU racing and desktop-icon activities depend on Task Manager, Explorer, display settings and Windows permissions. Eight interface-language options are available; some detailed content may fall back to Chinese or English. Translation, song recognition and news require internet access and their respective services. Translation sends selected text, and song recognition sends an audio sample. Availability depends on region, network and provider.

about: While you answer an email, a sunflower on your taskbar turns its head to follow your cursor.           Bloomline is a cozy desktop companion: a strip of soil right above your Windows taskbar. Your garden starts as one small mound with a single flower, and it stays out of your way: everywhere outside the garden, your clicks go straight through to your windows.  Water and grow  Pour the watering can over the soil and the garden gathers energy. Spend it to grow your plants by hand: raise a stem taller, branch it, swell a bud until it opens. Changed your mind? Snip it with the scissors and the energy comes back.          Collect seeds  Blooms ripen glowing seeds. Click them to collect, then spend them in the store on 14 more species, or on a bag of fertiliser that doubles a plant's growth, seeds and soil for a whole day.          Meet every plant  Every species has a life of its own. Mimosas fold their leaves as your cursor passes, flytraps snap shut on the flies that come to visit, bamboo clacks, and bellflowers ring a note each.  Dandelions wait for you to blow their seeds away, lavender calls butterflies to perch, tulips close for the night and four o'clocks open after dark with a soft glow.          Spread the soil  Healthy plants gather soil. Sprinkle it from the sack wherever you like and the garden spreads left along your taskbar, with room for as many plants as the soil can hold. Pick any colour for each species on a colour wheel.          Grow at your own pace  An idle garden at heart, it runs on your PC's clock and keeps growing while the game is closed. Look in for a minute between tasks or tend it for half an hour. Forgotten plants only wilt, and come back once watered: nothing is ever lost.  Made for your desktop   A transparent garden on top of your windows; clicks pass through everywhere else   Do Not Disturb and Hide Garden hotkeys for when you need the whole screen   Can hide itself from screen shares and recordings, plus a green screen backdrop for streamers   Light on your PC, with a low power mode when nothing moves   Single-player, for Windows

about: SLOW ORBIT is a small idle space war made for the unused bottom corner of your screen. It opens there automatically in a borderless, always-on-top window, so you can keep an eye on the fleet while you work, watch something or play another game.  The ships handle combat and planet conquest on their own. Jump in whenever you want: click the battlefield to add a few shots, or fire a heavy barrage. A barrage can rescue a close fight, but it burns part of your hull and can end a run if you get greedy.  Each conquered planet pays credits. Spend them on more income, harder hits, stronger armor, quicker repairs and other upgrades. If the fleet is destroyed, you return to the first planet and lose the credits and upgrades from that run. Your rank, cards and weapons stay with you, giving the next attempt a better start.  Promotions offer four choices at a time, so every expedition can develop differently. Later, you can begin a new departure and trade the current run for Legacy and another ship. Gear and career progress carry over, and every type of ship adds something different to the fleet.  Every fifth planet is an outpost. Every tenth is a bastion with shields and defensive guns. That is usually where an easy run stops being easy—and where one more upgrade or a well-timed barrage can make the difference.

FlintWilde is a desktop idle game that adheres to such concept, allowing players to experience such an adventure while working or studying on their computers  In the game, players will take on the role of a solitary witch, wandering alone in the wilderness, collecting all the items you need, and fighting monsters to obtain rarer items  And In such cycle of battles and survival, upgrade your level and explore new monster types and weapon enhance trees. name: Knead a Break
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: From its cozy bed, Knead watches over a human who sits too much. When you sit too long, this grumpy cat pops up to cause mischief. But it's smart: it senses your flow and waits for a natural pause to nudge you. It isn’t being naughty—it just wants to get you out of your chair so you can move around.
about: MEET KNEAD  Knead is a small Abyssinian with a permanently unimpressed face. It sprawls over a ball of yellow yarn in the corner of your Windows desktop, quietly watching over a human who spends a little too long at the computer.  Most of the time, it sleeps peacefully. But when it is time for a little movement, it knows exactly how to make itself noticed.  A LITTLE MISCHIEF, FOR A REASON  Knead is not another quiet notification.  It peeks over the edge of your window, or clings on and gives the window a tiny shake.  It steals a little attention on purpose—just enough to break through your focus and lure you away from your work for a moment. Each interruption is brief, playful, and unmistakably feline.  A FEW MINUTES, THEN BACK TO WORK  Interacting with Knead opens a compact guided-movement window. It demonstrates one simple, desk-friendly movement at a time, accompanied by a short instruction and timer.  A little stretch, a little movement, and a short break becomes a moment together. Afterwards, you can return to whatever you were doing.  A LITTLE MOVEMENT, A LITTLE GROWTH  Usually, Knead is the one looking out for you. You can look after it too, with a little food in its bowl and some fresh water beside it.  The moments you spend moving and caring for it help it grow, and find their way into your shared journal. Every now and then, you can turn back a few pages and see how much time you have spent together.  COME THE WEEKEND, IT HAS PLANS OF ITS OWN  On weekends and holidays, you can plan a little journey for Knead on its hand-drawn map. While you take some time away from work, it gets to see the world beyond your desktop.  A journey usually lasts a full weekend or holiday break. It will generally send a letter on the first day, letting you know how life on the road is treating it.  When it comes home, there will be mysterious gifts tucked away in its bag. What they are can wait until you are together again.  NOT NOW? A LITTLE LATER  When the timing is not right, Knead can wait a little longer. It goes back to rest for a while before coming to find you again.  The cat may be persistent, but it still knows when to give you room. The timing of the break remains in your hands.  QUIET COMPANY, TOO  For a meeting, screen sharing, or simply a little quiet, you can temporarily hide Knead and bring it back when you are ready.  Knead is not here to manage your day. It just wants to make taking a little break easier—and feel a little more like playing with a cat.

name: Desktop Pecks
lang: English
short: You are procrastinating, and your birds voice their opinions! An idle bird game that chills on your screen - grow a flock on a floating island, feed them, collect every species, and get roasted while you work!
about: On Linux, Transparent and Perch modes need a desktop with a compositor (KDE Plasma and GNOME both have one).     Are  YOU  chronically  GLUED  to your screen?   Your birds know exactly which app is in front, and they know exactly how long you've been playing games instead of doing homework!  They will roast you , with  sarcasm  and (sometimes cringe)  humor .     DESKTOP PECKS  is a cute  unhinged  idle bird game that lives on your screen! The big island floats above your desktop as you work, or you can shrink the big island into a  mini-island  and move it to the corner of your screen! The flock gets on with its day while you get on with yours - and they have a lot to say about you, who they refer to as  "the tall one" !   For privacy,  I don't collect any data , and all detection data never leaves your computer. In fact, the game can be played completely offline. There is also  NO GENERATIVE AI in game  - all detection logic and roasts are pre-defined, so no one except you and your birds know what you are doing.       Your birds  TALK  to each other, to the visitor birds, and  about you . They know things about you, such as what app is in front, how long you are gone, the current time, and so on! Most desktop pets just vibe quietly in a corner, but these birds chat about you, and sometimes, they even taunt you directly!                 The island can float over your screen with  no window frame  at all! ( Island is always-on-top of other windows by default, but you can change it in the settings )   PERCH Mode  shrinks the entire island down to  a single ELDER BIRD  chilling on a tiny tiny island.   CLICKING and TYPING  pass straight through the empty sky to the app behind the game, and you can always drag the island out of your way, so you can work or play other games while the birds chill!       You start with 2  budgies  and 2  cockatiels  in your house! Earn your way to unlock  street ,  meadow , and  volcano  (where the locals are a  dragon  and a  cinderfly ), and more to come.  Swipe  to switch the island   Each island is its own community, so each island  has its own birds for you to unlock and care for !                   Tap island  = grow food     Tap bird  =  feed  the birds, and they  peck the food  to produce... well...  Pecks ! You can spend  Pecks  to unlock upgrades, buy more birds, upgrade farms, and so much more!     Build farms  to produce food while you are gone! However, you must  encourage  those lazy farmer birds every day, or they would stop farming and starve the other birds!    Keep clicking to start a  combo , which gives you more per click!    Your farms will work and your birds peck  even if you close the game  and come back tomorrow.                   Every species is documented in a  BOOK .           Visitors  will show up every so often to give you a  HUGE  boost! There are even  rare visitors  that visit daily, giving you exotic rewards.                 The  PECK SHOP  has a huge list of permanent  upgrades  that unlock as you get close to affording them, such as "  Peer Pressure  ", "  Radioactive Flowers  ", "  Feudalism  ", and so on. You can also buy  exotic foods , and your birds will absolutely judge you (mostly positively) if you buy those!    Nothing in game costs real life money.       Misc Details     Supports Windows, macOS, and Linux.    No account, no ads, no in-app purchases.    Future updates will always be free.

name: Pixie - Desktop Pet That Mirrors You
lang: English, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Arabic, Simplified Chinese, Turkish, Japanese, Portuguese - Portugal, Russian
short: Pixie is a desktop pet that mirrors your face through your webcam in real time, in pixel art or hand-drawn ink. It obeys hand gestures, plays rock-paper-scissors, chats back and can be your face on stream. Seventeen characters with their own voices, and all vision runs locally.
about: Your desktop just adopted a pet — and it's copying your face.  Pixie is a crew of 17 tiny pixel companions that live on top of your windows. Turn your head, blink, talk, smirk — your pet mirrors you live through your webcam. Not a filter, not a video effect: a little creature with its own life, sitting at the bottom of your screen. IT MIRRORS YOU, LIVE Head direction, eye blinks, mouth, smiles, a raised eyebrow, even a frown — 🤨 right back at you. Powered by on-device vision that never touches the internet. RECORD A CLIP FOR REELS, TIKTOK AND SHORTS Hit record and Pixie films itself as a vertical 9:16 video with your voice. Talk and your pet talks along; pull a face and it pulls one back. Its own sounds, dances and @ character switches make it into the clip too. Up to three minutes in 1080p or 720p, on a dark, paper or green-screen background, saved straight to your Videos folder. Your camera image is never in it. Start it from settings or type /clip. IT TALKS WITH ITS PAWS ✌️ makes it dance, ☝️ drags it around the screen, ✊ a closed fist sends it to sleep, 🖐 an open palm wakes it up. Give it a 👍 and it purrs; a 👎 and it sulks. Smart filtering keeps everyday hand movement from setting it off. IT PLAYS ROCK-PAPER-SCISSORS Pump your fist three times and the game is on: a 3-2-1 countdown, then throw. Your pet reads your hand through the webcam, holds up its own pick on a little card and keeps score. It picks before you throw, so it can't cheat — and it gloats when it wins and sulks when it loses. IT REACTS TO SOUND A sudden clap or bang startles it; everyday talking doesn't. It is a little dramatic about this. IT CHATS BACK — AND REMEMBERS YOU Just open the chat window and talk — the language model ships inside Pixie, so there is no key to get, no account to make and no setup at all. Every character answers in its own personality. Optional local memory means your pet remembers your name, your jokes and your late-night sessions. All of it stays on your machine. TYPE IT, AND IT DOES IT Prefer the keyboard? Over twenty slash commands live in the chat window — /dance, /sleep, /rps, /theme pen, /size big, /camera off and more; /help lists them all. Type @dragon and the pet's pixels rearrange into the dragon, who takes over the conversation: @ works with every character and every theme, in your own language. DRAWN TWO WAYS Classic pixel art, or a hand-drawn pen style with a lively, wobbly ink line. Every character comes in both — switch any time in settings or with /theme. SEVENTEEN CHARACTERS, THIRTY-SIX LOOKS, SEVENTEEN VOICES Cat, dog, rabbit, panda, hamster, penguin, fox, owl, ghost, dragon, robot, slime, capybara, frog, duck, shark and octopus — each with at least two themes and its own voice: the cat meows, the dog woofs, the duck quacks, the robot beeps, the slime… bloops. The chat window recolours itself to match whoever you pick. Everything is included; there is nothing to unlock. (Sounds can be muted with one click.) IT HAS A LIFE OF ITS OWN Moods that shift with the time of day, spontaneous naps (it yawns first), sudden zoomies, and a purr when you click it. Ignore it for long enough and it taps on the glass with a paw — tap, tap. IT KNOWS WHEN YOU'RE AWAY Leave your desk and it notices: first it taps on the glass to check if you're still there, then it curls up for a nap. Come back and it wakes up, thrilled to see you. Then it stays up for a while to keep you company. IT MAKES ITSELF AT HOME Three sizes. Starts with Windows if you want it to. Lives in the system tray with one-click toggles for the camera and cursor following. No webcam, or camera switched off? It still trots along beside your mouse cursor, chats and obeys every command. The interface speaks ten languages. It's light on your PC, too: at rest it uses only a few percent of the CPU, even on a 2012 dual-core, and the chat model naps when you're not talking to it. Settings fit on one screen, too: click a tile to switch the camera, lip sync, pet sounds or gesture

name: Your "Thing"
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, French, German, Russian, Japanese, Traditional Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Korean
short: Finally, you can grow your own little thing. Water it, feed it, and experiment with your technique to shape how it grows. Every mushroom has its own size, patterns, and quirks. It lives right on your desktop, reacts to your touch, and sometimes gets up to mischief. How big will yours get?
about: Everyone deserves their own little thing.  And now, you can grow yours right on your desktop.   Your Thing  is a cute, quirky desktop mushroom pet with a little room for experimentation. Water it, feed it, and watch it grow. The order, timing, and technique of your care can all affect the final result.  Some grow beautifully. Some develop unusual patterns. And some might surprise you in ways you never expected.  Ready to see what yours becomes?  Grow It Your Way  Growing a mushroom takes more than a little water and fertilizer.  Experiment with different care routines, try different combinations, and discover how your choices affect its growth. The order and timing of your actions matter, so there's room to experiment and find your own approach.  Young mushrooms are easier to shape. As they mature, their features gradually settle into place.  A little patience goes a long way. So does knowing what you're doing.  Every Mushroom Has Its Own Character  Size, shape, patterns, and other features can vary from one mushroom to another.  Each one has its own look, and you can discover different results through experimentation. Collect the mushrooms you've raised and revisit your past creations in the collection.  After all, you put in the effort. You might as well keep a record of your finest work.  A Little Companion on Your Desktop  Your mushroom isn't just sitting there looking pretty.  Click it, drag it around, and see how it reacts. It'll follow your cursor with its eyes, fall asleep, wake up, and occasionally do something unexpected.  You can leave it quietly hanging out on your desktop while you work, or give it some attention whenever you need a little distraction.  You do your thing. It'll do its thing.  And sometimes, it'll get up to a little mischief.  What Can You Do?     Grow your own mushroom:  Water it, feed it, and experiment with different care routines.     Discover different results:  Explore how the order and timing of your actions affect growth.     Collect unique mushrooms:  Observe differences in size and patterns, and keep track of your past creations.     Interact with your companion:  Click, drag, and watch its various reactions.     Keep it on your desktop:  Let your little companion hang out while you go about your day.    So, how will you raise yours?  Give it some care, try a few things, and see what you end up with.  The final result depends on more than just natural talent. Your technique matters, too.

name: Desktop Bonsai Towns
lang: English, Japanese, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Indonesian, Ukrainian, Dutch, Greek, Swedish, Spanish - Latin America, Czech, Danish, Turkish, Norwegian, Hungarian, Finnish, Bulgarian, Vietnamese, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Polish, Malay, Romanian, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean
short: Two worlds: Cyberpunk Town and Fantasy Town. A tiny voxel bonsai grows on your desktop for hours while a city builds itself along its trunk and branches. Watch residents live their lives as storms, meteors and giant invaders strike. Unlock pruning shears and collect a variety of bonsai styles.
about: A city that grows on a bonsai Desktop Bonsai Towns is an observation sim. A voxel bonsai slowly grows in its pot, and a cyberpunk city builds itself on the trunk and branches: towers, sky bridges, neon signs, holographic ads, an elevated loop line and airships. You are the observer. Leave it running beside your work and glance over now and then.  Two worlds are available from the start: Cyberpunk Town and Fantasy Town. More themed worlds are planned. Put it on your desktop Desktop mode hides the background and the interface, so only the bonsai sits on top of your desktop. You can drag the pot anywhere on screen. The city keeps growing while you work in other windows. A living city   Little residents go about their lives in the city.   Factions form, split and absorb each other. A megacorp buys up buildings, a cult gathers followers, hackers black out whole blocks, and a security bureau cordons off trouble spots.   Changing weather, disasters and invasions bring surprises to the city, from acid rain and meteor strikes to mechanical spiders, sky pirates and, very rarely, a giant cat.   Everything is made of voxels, so blasts, fires and quakes tear the city apart block by block. Branches that lose their support fall, homes and all.   A light touch   Unlock pruning to cut branches with shears. New buds sprout from the cut and grow back.   Funds carry over between runs. Spend them on permanent unlocks: cars and flying cars, automatic defenses, cinematic and event cameras, photo mode and more.   Grow, finish, replant A bonsai takes several hours of real time to finish. Each run grows a bonsai in a traditional style, with rare wild variants. Finished trees go on your bonsai shelf, where you can view them in 3D, fill the collection and unlock new pots for the next planting. If the city falls, an end-of-days chronicle shows what went wrong and offers a hint for next time. Privacy The game does not connect to the internet except through the Steam client, for Steam Cloud saves, achievements and game updates.

about: Welcome to Your Hearthside    Hearthside: Your Custom Fireplace  is an ultra-customizable ambient fireplace simulator and cozy desktop productivity companion. Whether you need a warm backdrop while studying, reading, coding, or unwinding after a long day, Hearthside is designed to be your personal digital comfort zone.             Interactive Dynamic Islands & Productivity   Hearthside isn't just an idle screen—it's an interactive workstation companion featuring sleek, expandable  Dynamic Island widgets  that float gracefully over your hearth:     Pomodoro Focus Timer:  Boost your productivity with customizable focus sessions, short breaks, and long breaks with audio cues.     Interactive Task List:  Jot down daily to-dos, check off completed items, and drag-and-drop tasks to prioritize your day.     Custom Timers & Stopwatch:  Set quick alarms for water breaks, reminders, or track your work sprints.     Minimalist Clocks & Calendar:  Keep track of time with clean digital and analog clock faces.     Cozy Notes:  Keep quick reminders, inspirational thoughts, or scratchpad notes right beside the fire.     Dock, Drag & Resize:  Freely reposition, collapse into compact pills, or resize your islands to fit your workflow.               Desktop Companion Modes   Keep the fire burning while you work, browse, or play other games:     Floating Transparent Overlay:  Strip away the room and float a borderless, transparent fire directly over your desktop windows, IDE, or browser.     Docked Sidebar Mode:  Snap Hearthside to the left or right of your monitor like a dedicated sidebar dock, keeping your fire and productivity islands neatly stacked in view.     Always-on-Top Support:  Keep your cozy fire visible above all other active desktop windows.                             Deep Fireplace & Room Customization   Craft your dream fireplace down to the smallest detail:     50+ Wall Styles:  Cycle through dozens of wall textures across multiple material groups including Brick, Wood, Tile, Marble, Metal, and Festive.     Custom Wall Text & Quotes:  Write your own personal messages, favorite motivational quotes, or goals directly onto the brickwork in custom fonts and colors.     Custom Art Gallery & Slideshow:  Place your own photos or digital artwork on the wall. Display a single framed piece, or load a folder of images to cycle through a smooth carousel slideshow.     Fire & Smoke Dynamics:  Choose from multiple log arrangements, adjust fire size from a gentle glow to a roaring blaze, and fine-tune flame speed, opacity, smoke, and floating embers.     Full Color Control:  Customize the exact color of the flames, glowing coals, and walls using full RGB palettes.                               Ambient sounds & Audio   Layer immersive soundscapes to create your ultimate acoustic sanctuary:     Layered Nature Sounds:  Mix and match soothing background environments including thunderstorms, winter howling winds, peaceful creeks, rain and wilderness breezes.     Cozy Lo-Fi & Acoustic Soundtrack:  Enjoy hours of built-in curated music spanning Lo-Fi beats, Celtic folk, and peaceful Piano tracks.     Local Music Folder Player:  Point Hearthside to any folder on your PC to load and play your personal music collection directly through the in-game audio player.     Fire Acoustics:  Customize the volume and crackle tone of the burning logs.               Presets, Controls & Accessibility      Camera Angles:  Seamlessly switch between cinematic wide-room views, tight hearth close-ups, and cozy side perspectives.     Accessibility & Colorblind Support:  Built-in colorblind simulation LUT filters (Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia, Achromatopsia) with customizable intensity, UI scaling, and full keyboard/gamepad rebinding.             Roadmap & Future Updates   Hearthside continues to expand with new community-driven content:    Additional seasonal fireplace materials and seasonal room decor.    Expand

name: Your Desktop Companion - Lumi Demo
lang: English*, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Turkish*
short: Introducing Lumi: an AI that lives on your desktop.Lumi is a fully animated 3D AI companion who stays with you while you work, browse, play games, listen to music or just chill out.Instead of being a typical chatbot stuck in a browser window, Lumi is an interactive character who lives right on your Windows desktop.
about: Introducing Lumi: an AI that lives on your desktop.     Lumi is a fully animated 3D AI companion who stays with you while you work, browse, play games, listen to music or just chill out.    Instead of being a typical chatbot stuck in a browser window, Lumi is an interactive character who lives right on your Windows desktop.     She Watches With You     Say "Look At My Screen" to get a quick look. Or "Watch My Screen" and she'll join you while you're gaming, or watching something. Lumi can see what's on your screen and help you choose a card. Celebrate a boss wave! Or comment on a video.    She can read what's on your screen, help you pick a card, cheer at a boss wave and comment on the video you're watching.    Screen watching is off until you turn it on, and everything she sees is processed on your PC.    In demanding games, Game Mode automatically pauses her AI so your GPU can focus on your game.                              An Ongoing Relationship   Chat with Lumi by text or voice, and your relationship grows over time.    She remembers important things from your previous conversations.    She notices when you've been away.    She warms up to you and gets more familiar the more time you spend together.                 Powered by Local AI   Lumi's core AI runs locally on your PC. Her brain (the language model), her ears (speech recognition), her voice and her memory all run on your own computer, without a constant connection to a cloud AI.    Pick the brain that fits your PC, from lightweight to high-end.    A starter brain and voice come included.                She Responds to Your Music     Lumi can hear the audio playing on your PC.    She picks up rhythm, energy, bass and beats in real time.    Play some music and watch her move along to whatever you're listening to.                 Expressive & Interactive     She breathes, blinks and follows your cursor with her eyes.    She blushes, reacts emotionally and loves a good head pat.    Her moods and behavior shift with the conversation, the music and your relationship.                      More Than Just Conversation   When enabled, she can:    Open apps, folders and links.    Search the web or YouTube.    Control media playback and system volume.    Set timers and reminders, and read them out loud when they're due.    She can only use these supported actions, and nothing runs until you confirm it.              She Speaks Your Language     Chat with Lumi in English, Turkish, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, Russian, Japanese, Korean or Simplified Chinese.       The interface is available in all of these languages.    Her voice and voice input work best in English.              Privacy by Design     Lumi's core AI runs locally on your PC.    Screen watching, microphone input, system audio and desktop actions are all off until you turn them on.    Sensitive conversation content is kept out of release logs.    Every desktop action goes through strict safety and validation checks.             Your desktop isn't just where Lumi runs.      It's her home.

name: Desktop Legends Demo
lang: English
short: Desktop Legends is an idle desktop action game featuring fantasy character progression, incremental resource management, and visual customization. Help your hero take their legendary stand against the forces of darkness right on your desktop!
about: Desktop Legends is an interactable battlefield for your desktop. Move and resize to your preference and watch your hero carve a legend through their enemies.                   Progression happens on your time, with no penalties for being engrossed in your work, or needing a bathroom break. Amass coins while the hero fights for you, then spend those to advance the game state.                     Use the coins dropped by enemies to enhance your hero's power, level up your enemies, and unlock powerful divine interventions. Each upgrade adds the potential for you to vanquish more enemies or earn more coins.                     Change the vibes to match your style. Unlock custom, hand-drawn decorations to swap to a fresh look at any time. Mix and match backdrops, heroic banners, and more to create your perfect arena.                     Combine forces with your hero to make a stand worthy of song! You are the divine intervention keeping your hero from succumbing to the hordes of enemies. Drop meteors, shake goblins for loose change, and more!  This demo includes:    One desktop hero    Two full customization sets    Four unique enemies to unlock    Four interactive interventions

name: Desktop Gensokyo: Auto Dodging, Dinner at Six
lang: English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese
short: Reimu, Marisa, Cirno — 15 girls from Gensokyo now live on your desktop. Pat their heads, watch them chat and bicker, or open the shrine and let them blast danmaku while you work. The spell cards keep flying and the kitchen stays busy whether you're watching or not.
about: ⛩ The girls of Gensokyo have moved onto your desktop  They wander along the bottom of your screen, keeping you company through work, late nights, and everything in between. You don't have to do a thing — just pat one on the head now and then.  • 15 companions: Reimu Hakurei, Marisa Kirisame, Cirno, Aya Shameimaru, Sakuya Izayoi, Patchouli Knowledge, Hong Meiling, Youmu Konpaku, Reisen Udongein Inaba, Alice Margatroid, Sanae Kochiya, Koishi Komeiji, Yukari Yakumo, Yuyuko Saigyouji, Remilia Scarlet.  • Tap to pat — each girl has her own voice and her own way of responding. They sit down when tired, raise their hands when happy.  • Every character has unique desktop events: Reimu rattles her donation box, Marisa "borrows" your coins and runs, Cirno challenges you to a duel, Aya shoves a newspaper in your face, Meiling dozes off mid-shift, and Koishi appears on the other side of your screen without warning. Respond and earn small gifts and affection.  • Two characters standing near each other will start talking: Sakuya catching Meiling slacking, Yuyuko calling Youmu "I'm hungry~", Cirno picking a fight with Marisa — 21 pairs of exclusive two-person dialogues.  • Morning greetings when you start your PC, meal reminders, and late-night check-ins if you're still up.  🎴 Auto danmaku idling — spell cards one after another  Open the shrine in the bottom corner and your team fires automatically, dodges bullets on their own, and farms fairies and fur-balls for faith. Cards can be leveled up — the longer you play, the stronger they get.  • Each character has her own danmaku style: Reimu's homing seals, Marisa's straight magic blasts, Aya's wind gusts, Sakuya's throwing knives, Alice's dolls.  • Spell cards auto-trigger when spirit fills up — 30 cards total: Dream Sign "Duplex Barrier", Love Sign "Master Spark", Perfect Freeze, Sakuya's World, Shanghai Doll, Present World Slash, and more.  • Level up spell cards with Faith (levels 1–10, +15% damage per level) to keep pace with later waves.  • Cards chain together: freeze then burn for 3× shatter damage; seal then strike for 2× combo; soak then freeze for longer CC. Order your declarations and watch the damage snowball.  • Max-bond pairs declare Union Spell Cards together — 10 combinations: Dream Spark, Netherworld Twin Dance, Twin Miko Seal, and more.  • Every 5 waves, a Boss arrives: Rumia, Wriggle Nightbug, Kogasa Tatara, Akyuu Motoori. Survive without taking a hit within the time limit and capture her spell card — each one grants a permanent bonus to your whole team. 8 Boss spell cards to collect.  • The desktop characters are Q-style chibi art; the shrine battle uses pixel sprites. Both Illustration are original to this game.  ⭐ Summon companions and grow stronger over time  • Pray at the shrine: draw a Great Blessing to summon a new companion; other draws give ingredients. 50 draws guarantee a Great Blessing; every 10-pull brings at least one new companion.  • No rarity tiers. Every companion starts at 1 star and grows naturally — affection rises, stars follow, up to 6 stars max. A few hours of idling gains a star.  • Each companion has four stats — attack, HP, defense, and speed. Luck shapes the food and gifts they find. The same character feels a little different for every player.  • Yukari Yakumo, Yuyuko Saigyouji, and Remilia Scarlet rarely appear at the shrine — but when they do, they arrive at 3 or 4 stars.  • Summoning a companion you already have gives her a large boost of growth experience.  🍙 The shrine kitchen — everyone takes a turn at the stove  • Once your battle roster is full, companions resting on the desktop rotate through kitchen shifts — four burners, eight seats. They cook whatever the hungry ones are craving.  • When a dish is done, the chef carries it over herself and hands it to the companion who was hungry. The recipient cheers up, and the bond between the two of them deepens.  • 12 original dishes tied to Gensokyo locat

name: PeeCee Critters
lang: English
short: A tiny critter lives on your taskbar while you work. Click it and a whole monster-collecting RPG opens up: nearly 200 critters to catch, train and evolve, fourteen lands with a story to put right, five islands out at sea, and a real ending. Buy once: no energy, no ads, no paid extras.
about: PeeCee Critters is a desktop pet with a whole monster-collecting RPG inside it.  A tiny pixel critter lives along the bottom of your screen — walking, napping and wandering your taskbar while you work.   New in the 1.0 update:     A story to the end: a Dimming in every land to put right, an ending with credits, and a true ending after it    Five outer isles by ferry, each with its own warden, rooms and house rule    Wren, a rival who meets you on the road    Treasure maps cut from your own world, a night market, notice-board jobs at the last inn    Your own boat on the open sea, once the isles are put right    Seven forms to earn, among them TIDEWORN and LONGLIT    Friend duels and raids through Steam, and leaderboards for the mini-games       Every so often a wild critter turns up beside your pet. Click your pet and the CritterScope opens over whatever you were doing. Win, and you're a step closer to recording it.         Nearly 200 critters  to find across  a hundred evolution lines  and eleven types, with rare forms: a spectre after dark, a prism once in a very long while.             Walk a world of  fourteen lands , each walled off by fog and held by an  alpha . Bring three to the fight, and the alpha changes type halfway down. Every save gets its own continent.             Level them, evolve them, and earn rare finishes over hundreds of wins.  Over 100 crests  mark what you've done, and some of them are secret. Build up an island of your own.                  Recolour the device and choose how big your pet is. Then put your best six on an animated brag card to send someone.                Buy once: no energy, timers, ads or paid extras. Glints are earned by playing, never bought    No account. Friend duels, raids and leaderboards go through Steam; everything else works offline    A small download, made to be left running all day          Will it get in my way?  It steps aside when a fullscreen game or video covers its screen, and Ctrl+Alt+H hides the pet whenever you like.   I have more than one monitor.  Choose which display it lives on.   Keyboard or mouse?  Either. Everything on the device can be clicked, and any button can have a key of your choosing.   Is there a demo?  Yes: the first three lands (THE COMMONS, FOREST and SWAMP) and their alphas, free.

name: Glims
lang: English, Spanish - Spain, Portuguese - Brazil, French, German, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Russian
short: A battle pet that lives on your desktop. Your glims walk your taskbar, live in a 3D house you decorate and earn gold on their own. When you call, they hold off an invasion on your screen or dive a 20-floor dungeon. Free, light, and it works offline.
about: A battle pet that lives on your desktop — and has a house.  Glims don't live inside a window. They walk your taskbar, climb the edges of your programs, sit down, doze off and chat with each other while you work. When you call, the game happens on your screen — not in a fullscreen window on top of it. It never steals focus, never covers what you're doing, and disappears with one click.  THE HOUSE  A small, transparent isometric 3D house in the corner of your screen. Eleven rooms to buy with in-game gold: they rest in the living room, sleep in the bedroom and cook in the kitchen; in the office, workshop, training area, storeroom, game room, lab, dungeon and arena they work, earn gold and get tired. Every room has its own catalogue — over three hundred pieces in all. Each piece of furniture is one unit: for two beds, buy two. Place a piece and a glim walks over to build it, hammer in hand, and it stays blue until it's done. The HOUSE button shows every room live, in a hive view, with how much each one earns per minute.  FOUR MODES, ALL ON YOUR SCREEN    Jade Castle  — the twenty-floor dungeon. Build a squad of up to three and go down floor by floor; the fight runs itself, enemies have special moves, and every five floors there's a boss. After it, the only question that matters: leave with the loot, or go one deeper? Whoever falls stays down, and anything not banked is lost.   Invasion  — a jade lawn assembles over your desktop and invaders come in from the right, lane by lane. Plant your glims to hold them: sword up close, bow and magic at range. Cards drop on the lawn and fly to your hand with a click.   Challenge  — a boss at the top of the screen pours magic down and you dodge by dragging your glim with the mouse; it shoots on its own. Six bosses in rotation, four fury phases, bonuses falling from above and a rank from S to D. Grazing spells without getting hit scores points.   Arena  — a 3v3 squad duel with gold on the line, paid out in glimbucks: the currency of the coloured chests.   Play three modes in one day to close the daily mission.  TEN GLIMS TO COLLECT  Each with its own card, stats and way of fighting. Weapons are real 3D models, fitted to the hand — or stowed on the back, for those who fight with claw and magic. Special weapons are numbered: every piece carries its own serial, unique in the world. Swap one in your inventory and see the difference on screen right away.  SEASONS AND PRESTIGE  Every eight weeks a season begins: gold earned, kills, floors and wins turn into points, and reaching a hundred earns the season title. Accumulated prestige raises what your house earns.  BUILT FOR EVERYONE TO PLAY  Remappable keys, a colourblind mode with three types and adjustable strength, interface size from 80% to 160%, and soft effects for anyone bothered by screen shake and flashes. You can play with the mouse alone.  FREE, LIGHT AND OFFLINE  The game is free and runs without a connection. It's light, stays open all day and doesn't get in the way of what you're doing. Purchases are optional and fixed: packs with the contents listed — nothing random costs money. Chests, furniture and rooms are bought with gold earned by playing.

name: The Long Drift
lang: English, Korean
short: Build, upgrade, and watch your tiny universe evolve.
about: About This Game   Explore the vast universe from your desktop.  This is a desktop exploration game that runs quietly in a corner of your screen while you go about your day.  Travel between planets, space stations, and resource zones, gathering materials and expanding your reach across the cosmos.            Explore, build, and go beyond  Discover new planets, harvest resources, and upgrade your equipment to build more advanced spacecraft.  Complete quests, build colonies on distant planets, and start fresh with a stronger ship.  As technology evolves, Break past the speed of light and face all kinds of unexpected encounters.  Always on, never in the way  Even when you’re idle, the universe keeps moving—ships travel, resources grow, and exploration continues. The game stays unobtrusive on your desktop while your journey unfolds in the background.  Play your way  Let the universe run entirely on its own, or step in whenever you want to make decisions and change your course.

name: Tide & Tails
lang: English, Japanese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, French, German, Simplified Chinese
short: A cozy desktop idle fishing game made to keep you company. Fish, collect, and display your favorite fish while you work or study. Upgrade your gear, explore new waters, and let your journal record the journey.
about: Welcome to Tide & Tails  Place your little boat in a corner of your desktop. Let the fishing quietly continue while you work or study, then come back whenever you have time to see what you’ve caught today.  Explore Different Waters  Set out from a peaceful river, explore new waters, and discover new fish along the way.  Complete Your Fish Collection  Catch all kinds of fish and gradually complete your collection. Upgrade your gear and search for rarer fish.  Build Your Little Aquarium  Bring your favorite fish back to your aquarium and decorate your own little underwater world, making it richer and more lively over time.  Keep Your Own Tide & Tails Journal  Your journal records the catches, discoveries, and progress from your journey. You can also write down your own thoughts, feelings, and anything you want to remember.  This is more than just a record of your progress in the game. It can also become a personal journal of your own.

name: Farmer=nil
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: Farmer = nil is a programming-based automation farm right on your computer screen! Write scripts for your robots, collect resources, unlock tech, and build the most efficient farm.
about: Farmer = nil    is an automated farming game that lives in the corner of your screen.    Use the Lua programming language to automate your crops. Hit "run," watch your farm tend itself, and enjoy the satisfaction that comes with total automation.           Game Features   An idle desktop companion that stays in the corner of your screen.    Write your own Lua scripts to build an efficient farm.    No pressure, no time-limited tasks, and no penalties for failure.

name: Bird Feeder
lang: English
short: A relaxing idle bird-watching game for your desktop. A thin garden sits above your taskbar while you work, and real birds drop by: set out seed, pet your visitors, and fill your Bird Book with their songs and calls.
about: Bird Feeder is a cozy idle bird-watching game: a thin strip of garden that lives just above your taskbar.    Pour a cup of tea, get on with your day, and real birds of the Pacific Northwest will drop by to visit.    Glance down now and then: a chickadee pecking at the tray, a jay after the peanuts, and maybe a new page waiting in your Bird Book.                 44 birds of the Pacific Northwest  to get to know, and 2 rare strays. Each newcomer leaves a sealed page in your Bird Book.  Hear a bird sing or call in the garden, and its page plays it back with a sonogram.                        Set out a little food  and see who comes: sunflower seed for chickadees, peanuts for jays, suet for woodpeckers, nectar for hummingbirds and mealworms for robins.  Every visit earns a few stars. The crow, for the record, is not fussy.               Spend your stars on new foods, more feeders, a berry shrub, a water dish, a birdhouse and native trees. New food and new homes bring new birds.               Set every tree and feeder wherever it looks right, add a gnome, a lantern or a pot of cosmos, and give your garden its own name.              Pet a bird and the view leans in close, with little hearts. Some birds love it, and the shy ones need a softer touch.              The more days a bird comes back, the more its page grows, until it wears the gold band of a familiar visitor.  Now and then one leaves a feather, a seed husk or a pine cone, a keepsake for your Cabinet.               Birds splash in the pond, a Rufous chases an Anna's from the nectar, and in summer a robin fledgling begs to be fed.               Each season lasts a real week and brings its own visitors. When rain comes, the small birds tuck in under the pine.                      At night the small birds sleep in the pine, the Barred Owl calls from its snag, and a moth or two circles your lantern.               Step away for a while, and a little postcard tells you what you missed, but only when there is news.                Field cards  are small seasonal goals, like "See a Northern Flicker on the lawn on 3 days." They never expire.             No timers, no chores and no punishment for being away.  No internet needed, and in our tests it uses about 2% of one CPU core.       Bird Feeder was made with AI. The game's code, the pixel art (every bird, prop and background) and the in-game text (species notes, tips and menus) were written or drawn by AI agents (Claude Code).  The music was generated with ElevenLabs (Eleven Music).  Every sound effect and bird call is synthesized in code written by AI agents. The bird calls are interpretations, not field recordings of real birds: they were tuned against measurements of real recordings, and no recording ships in the game. All of this content was made before release and ships inside the game. Nothing is generated while you play, and the game has no live AI features.   More features are under development:   You will be able to see bird spots in new locations such as Japan, Bali, and more...

name: Crashpad: Cozy Idle Outpost
lang: English
short: A cozy idle outpost that sits in a corner of your desktop and keeps running while you work. Your ship crash-landed on a floating rock and two little robots made it out. Build a base from the wreck, collect a fleet of little ships and send them into the fog.
about: Crashpad is a cozy idle game made to sit on your desktop. Shrink your outpost into a small widget in the corner of your screen and it keeps building and producing, and your ships keep flying, while you work, browse or watch something. Check in when a ship comes home.  Your ship came down hard. It won't fly again. But two little robots made it — and this crash pad is home now.  Now you're stranded on a little floating rock at the edge of nowhere. Start from the wreck, build a cozy outpost one building at a time, and send your ships out into the fog to see what's out there.  A little outpost on your desktop         Switch to widget mode and your outpost becomes a small floating island in the bottom-right corner of your screen — borderless, always on top, with a transparent background. Drag it anywhere and resize it to fit.  Choose whether the widget shows your base or the map.  Ships come and go while you work. When crates arrive, click them to collect and send the ship straight back out.  It stays out of your way: the music switches off, sounds can be set to alerts only or off, and the widget runs at a low frame rate to keep your PC free for work.  The widget remembers where you left it.         Build a cozy outpost         Raise Dew Collectors, Foundries, Fuel Condensers and Garden Domes to keep Water, Alloy, Fuel and Food flowing.  Build several of each production building, and upgrade your buildings — including the cargo pods that store everything.  Little helper bots bustle around the base while windows glow, fans spin and chimneys puff.  Your outpost keeps working while the game is closed, until its storage fills up. Come back and collect.   Collect a fleet         Send the quick Courier, the roomy Hauler and the curious Surveyor out on runs, then watch them lift off and land back at the dock.  Every ship gets its own little tab along the bottom of the screen — see who's ready, who's out and who's on the way home at a glance.  Each ship has a job — cargo, express or survey — and a look all its own.  Bring home blueprint fragments and build new ships from them.  Fill in your Codex one ship at a time.   Chart the fog         Send ships across a hex map of tiny asteroid outposts and watch the clouds part over places like Scrap Shallows, Fizz Canyon and Chime Ridge.  Chart new regions to raise your Survey Rank and make room for more buildings.  Now and then, a friendly space whale drifts by.   There are no loot boxes.

name: Guildlands - Artificer Class
lang: English, Spanish - Latin America, Japanese, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, French, German, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Indonesian
short: A new class for Guildlands. The Artificer fights by throwing flasks: fire across the whole row and acid that breaks armor. Their potions restore 30% more and come back sooner, and their spells spend emberblooms and jars of slime instead of runes.
about: Fire and acid in a flask The Artificer fights by throwing flasks.  Fire Flask  burns the whole row of enemies, and  Corrosive Cloud  breaks the armor of every enemy and covers them in acid that no armor can stop. Steady Hand Potions in the Artificer's slot restore 30% more, and the next one waits fewer fights to be ready. Their two own spells spend emberblooms, from Herbalism, and jars of slime instead of runes. Another way to play Guildlands' 15 classes stay free. The Artificer is not stronger than them: it's another way to fight, with its own trait and its own spells.      What's included   The  Artificer  class: create characters of this class.   Its trait,  Steady Hand .   Two class spells:  Fire Flask , dropped by a boss, and  Corrosive Cloud , earned through a quest.    960 emberblooms  to get started, once per account.

name: Finger Prison
lang: English, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Portuguese - Portugal, Korean
short: A keyboard-driven incremental desktop companion. Turn everyday typing into a tiny prison, collect equipment, and build chain reactions across your keys. Let the inmates keep you company, then return to experiment with your next build.
about: If you feel imprisoned at your keyboard too, at least you’ll have company.      Your keyboard just became a prison Finger Prison is a keyboard-driven incremental desktop companion. Keep it running while you work, chat, or browse, and your everyday keystrokes bring a tiny, darkly comic prison to life. Admit inmates, produce and sell reports, then invest the proceeds in your next equipment build. Type through your day. Come back with a plan. Each key is a cell you can manage. Unlock rooms, place equipment, and watch how one keystroke triggers nearby rooms and other gadgets. Experiment with more than 100 equipment items to turn ordinary typing into automatic effects and chain reactions. Build around placement, elements, and fusion Move equipment between rooms and combine Poison, Fire, Frost, and Lightning effects. Upgrade rooms to fit more equipment and choose materials for fusion. You can leave the prison beside your work, then return whenever you want to refine your little production line. A strange little operation of your own Collect inmates, reports, and evidence. Make the prison yours with room skins, inmate outfits, and surveillance-monitor frames. Cartoon reactions and dark humor give each keystroke a touch of absurdity. Big reactions. Small window. Arrange your build in the full keyboard view, or switch to a compact surveillance window in the corner of your desktop. Background input can be adjusted in Settings.    Single-player: keyboard for action, mouse for managing rooms and equipment.   Keep the game running to progress. There are no offline earnings.   Interface available in English, Simplified Chinese, German, Japanese, Korean, French, Spanish, and Portuguese.   Contains cartoon violence and dark humor.

name: Guildlands - Founder's Pack
lang: English, Spanish - Latin America, Japanese, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, French, German, Simplified Chinese, Korean
short: For those who are here from the start: the Founder's Steed, the Founder's Cape and Tunic (+10% magic find), your name in bronze with the bronze star, and 20% faster walking. Only on sale during the first month after launch.
about: For those who arrive first The Founder's Pack is for those who step into Aurelia from the very beginning. It's only on sale during the first month after launch: after that it doesn't come back, and its steed, cape, tunic and star can't be obtained any other way.      The Founder's Steed A bronze horse that only founders ride. It runs just like the common horse: no edge, only the pride of having been here from day one. It stays on your account, passes between your characters and is ridden with the Riding Permit I. Let everyone see who came first Your name shows in bronze, with the bronze star beside it, for everyone to see. You wear the Founder's Cape and Tunic, worn only by those who backed Guildlands from its earliest days. And you walk the world 20% faster.      What's included    The Founder's Steed : a bronze horse kept on your account. It runs like the common horse and is ridden with the Riding Permit I.    The Founder's Cape , kept on your account.    The Founder's Tunic : chest armor with +10% magic find, for one character and kept on your account.    Your name in bronze  with the  bronze star  beside it.    +20% walking speed  across the world.

name: Saju Friend
lang: English, Japanese, Korean, Spanish - Spain, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Ukrainian
short: A cozy pixel luck cat that lives in the corner of your screen while you work or study. Run a 15, 25 or 50-minute focus timer with 16 calm music tracks, crack fortune cookies and draw tarot on breaks, and dress up your cat and its corner with 63 outfits and room items. For entertainment only.
about: A cozy luck cat for your desktop Saju Friend is a desktop companion. Boknyang, a small pixel luck cat, sits on a cushion in the corner of your screen and stays on top while you work, study or browse. Clicks pass through around the cat, so it never gets in your way. Click the cat to open the menu, drag it to move it, and change its size from the right-click menu or with Ctrl + mouse wheel. Focus with your cat    Focus timer : pick 15, 25 or 50 minutes. Finish a session and the cat pays you Bokjeon, the in-game currency (rewards for up to 8 sessions a day). Quit early and the cat just looks a little sad.    16 background music tracks : lo-fi study, rainy night, jazz café, winter fireplace, dawn piano, city pop, forest breeze, bouncy 8-bit and calm Korean instruments such as gayageum and daegeum. Switch tracks or turn the music off any time.    Luck Orb : it slowly fills while the app is running and catches up for up to 2 hours while it is closed. Pop it to collect Bokjeon.   A little luck between tasks    Daily fortune and tarot : crack a fortune cookie, read today's luck line, or pick face-down tarot cards (one, two, three or five, your choice). The daily two-card reading counts once a day.    Luck from around the world : Western zodiac, Chinese zodiac, numerology, omikuji (shake the box until a stick pops out), Celtic tree, Maya day sign (nawal) and a one-line saju (Korean four-pillars) reading from your birth date.    Name compatibility : type two names and watch the number count up and stop. Korean stroke counts, Japanese kana and kanji, or the FLAMES game for English names. Names are not saved or sent anywhere.    Quick luck games : coin toss, dice, slots, scratch ticket and a ten-toss luck experiment, played with Bokjeon only. When a result is poor, tie it to a tree branch and shake it off.   Dress up the cat and its corner    63 outfits and room items : skins, hats, neckwear and auras for the cat, plus Bokjeon baskets, luck orbs, lanterns, cushions and clouds for its corner. You start with 10 and unlock the rest with Bokjeon and levels earned by playing.    Collect : a luck-play collection book with 17 common, rare and legendary entries, fortune cookie notes and slot symbols.   Light on your PC A small window, a frame rate that drops when idle, and keys read only in the name and amount boxes. Your birth date and play records are saved only on your PC and are never sent anywhere. Languages: Korean, English, Japanese, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Ukrainian, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese. For entertainment only Fortunes, saju, tarot, name compatibility and every luck game in this app are made for fun. They do not predict real events, and nothing here is advice about money, health, work or relationships. Coin, dice, slots and scratch tickets use only Bokjeon, the in-game currency. Bokjeon has no real-world value and cannot be bought. There is no real money, no purchases and no prizes. Animations only show a result that is already decided; they do not change the odds. Odds and payouts are shown on screen. AI-generated content disclosure Most of the 2D pixel art (the cat companion, its outfits and in-between animation frames, fortune-game icons, tarot cards, items and backgrounds) was first generated with AI image tools (PixelLab and an image-generation model), then retouched by hand by our designer. The background music tracks were generated with an AI music model (ACE-Step) and selected and edited by our developer. Sound effects are generated by the game's own code, not by AI. AI was used only during development. While you play, no AI runs inside the game, nothing new is generated, and the game never connects to an AI service. short: Turn your desktop into a slowly growing water oasis. Typing and everyday PC use generate Inspiration to unlock creatures, boats, decorations, and rare finds. Let it grow quietly while you work, then return to arrange the world and play with drifting objects through real-time water physics.
about: Welcome to Desktop Oasis             Demo Note: This demo focuses on Desktop Oasis's core desktop operation, Inspiration progression, water interaction, and collection experience. Some content scale, long-term progression, collections, and expanded features are still in development and testing; some features described below may not be enabled in the demo.      Turn Your Desktop into a Growing Water World    Desktop Oasis  is a small living water world designed to stay beside you during everyday PC use.  As you type, browse, work, or simply use your computer, you gradually generate  Inspiration .  Spend it to discover new creatures, plants, boats, decorations, and all kinds of curious little things, slowly turning a simple oasis into a richer world.     Use Your PC → Gain Inspiration → Discover New Things → Grow Your Oasis      You Do Your Thing. It Keeps Growing.   You do not need to stare at the game or click constantly.  Desktop Oasis can quietly stay beside your desktop and continue progressing while you work, study, browse the web, or handle other tasks.  Come back whenever you feel like playing.  See what you have gained, unlock something new, rearrange the world—or simply do nothing and watch little things drift across the water.               The Water Is Not Just a Background   The water here does more than look pretty.  Boats, logs, rafts, creatures, and other floating objects can drift, move, collide, and interact with the surrounding world.  Drag objects into the water, change their position, watch them move with the surface, or place different objects together and see what happens.  These small physical interactions make Desktop Oasis feel more like a living miniature water world than a looping animated wallpaper.               From Open Water to Your Own Oasis   As you keep discovering new content, you can gradually obtain more creatures, plants, boats, decorations, environmental objects, and special collectibles.  Place what you like in the world, adjust the layout and viewpoint, and let the same body of water slowly become your own.  The world is not packed with everything from the beginning.   Filling it is part of the progression.                Discover, Collect, and Complete Your Encyclopedia   As your world grows, there are always more things left to discover.  Unlock encyclopedia entries, find less common content, hunt for rare collectibles, and gradually fill out the world.  Every new discovery adds one more piece to your oasis.  Some special discoveries can also become Steam Inventory collectibles, extending part of your collection beyond the oasis itself.               It Can Be a Game—or Simply Stay Beside You   You can actively arrange, interact, and collect, or use Desktop Oasis as a long-running desktop companion.  It can run beneath your desktop, and it also supports windowed, borderless, and fullscreen presentation.  Watch the water move,  listen to ambient sounds or white noise,  drop in now and then to see what has changed,  or simply let it stay quietly beside you while you work or study.  The game also includes a dedicated low-resource mode for background use, designed to reduce system resource usage during long sessions.  It does not demand your full attention all the time.     Take a breath, open Desktop Oasis, and let a little digital calm accompany your day.           🌐 Gameplay & Features    Desktop Oasis blends a Desktop Companion, Idle Game, Incremental Game, Typing Game, Cozy / Relaxing Game, Collecting Game, encyclopedia progression, real-time water physics, an Interactive Desktop, a Virtual Ecosystem, a Miniature World, dynamic water scenery, background progression, and focus-friendly play. name: Deskside Days
lang: English, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese
short: A little bunny has moved onto your desktop. While you work or study, it lives its own small life in a corner of your screen, learning new skills and growing. In your free time, dress it up, decorate its home, and browse letters and travel photos. Glance over now and then for a small surprise.
about: A tiny island floats in a corner of your desktop, and a little bunny lives there. It has its own day to get through: busy with this and that, out for a stroll, and off to bed when it's tired.  While you write, sit in meetings, or play other games, you don't need to keep an eye on it or plan its day. Glance over when you're done and see how its day went.  You do your thing. It does its own.               This bunny can't sit still. It picks up new skills and keeps practicing, getting a little better each time. One moment it's busy at the stove, the next it may be off to the water with a fishing rod.  You don't have to teach it step by step or stay by its side. Just check in now and then to see what it's been practicing and how far it's come. Small skills add up over time. The bunny's in no hurry, and you don't need to be either.               This part is up to you. Furniture indoors and out can be placed and rotated freely: lay a rug by the window, put the piano next to the bookshelf, fly a kite above the yard. No need to finish in one go. Change a little whenever you feel like it, and the island slowly becomes the place you want.       Its look is yours to decide too. Mix and match hats, backpacks, tops, shoes and accessories, and choose a fur color such as snow white, cream, cocoa or mist gray. Put sunglasses on it and it will carry on with its day, not the least bit shy.               Most days on the island are ordinary. But one day you might look up and catch a spirit rising from the pond, and some nights the bunny heads off to the Dragon Palace.  They don't announce themselves. If you happen to see one, stay and watch for a bit.            Neighbors drop by for a visit and write to the bunny after they go home. These friends are all characters in the game, so there's no friend list to fill and nobody to wait for online.  The bunny keeps a diary, and the calendar records the days as they pass. It also travels to gardens, the seaside and pastry shops, takes photos with friends and keeps them in an album. Flip through it after a while and you'll find the island has collected quite a few stories.               Cherry blossoms in spring, summer nights made for looking up, autumn leaves across the yard, winter snow blanketing the island. Day and night each have their own look. The island changes with the days, and as long as you keep it open, it will share them with you.  When you finally look up from your work, it may have just finished too.

name: Lowtown
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Spanish - Latin America, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Turkish, Japanese
short: A tiny pixel-art village lives right above your Windows taskbar and grows all on its own — from the first tents to a city of skyscrapers — through days, nights and seasons. You just watch: clicks pass straight through, and the village fades away when your cursor comes near.
about: Lowtown is a tiny pixel-art village that lives right above your Windows taskbar. It is a fully autonomous desktop companion: you don't build anything and you don't give orders. The villagers live their own lives — just glance down now and then to see what they are up to.         A village that lives on its own  Villagers chop wood, fish, farm, bake bread, forge tools and put up new houses. The village council decides who takes on which trade as the settlement grows, and a little thought bubble pops up whenever someone starts something new. Children play outside, and newcomers arrive from beyond the edge of the screen.          From the first tents to skyscrapers  The settlement grows through seven eras — from a camp around a campfire to a village, a town, an industrial city and finally a metropolis. Canvas tents give way to timber cottages, brick houses and towers of steel and glass. When the whole strip is lined with skyscrapers, the town celebrates with fireworks — then you can start a new world or let the city live on.  Days, nights and seasons  A day passes in 24 minutes: the sun and the moon cross the sky, windows light up in the evening, and the village falls asleep at night.          A year lasts just 12 days. Spring blossom, summer greenery, autumn leaves and winter snow follow one another. Winter is the hardest season: villagers stock up on firewood and food, and children have snowball fights.         Stays out of your way    Clicks pass right through the village. It never takes focus and doesn't show up in Alt+Tab.    The village fades out when your cursor comes close.    Everything is in the tray icon: show or hide the village, choose the monitor, change the speed and language, start with Windows.    Light on resources: low frame rate, below-normal priority and Windows efficiency mode.    Your village is saved automatically.    Cozy by design  No combat, no disasters, no deaths and no way to fail. A hard winter only slows the village down — it never punishes you. Lowtown is made to keep you quiet company for hours while you work or study.

about: Bu About This Game:  Welcome to the most questionable fast-food joint you will ever run.  Totally Normal Meat Co. is a persistent idle farming and management simulator that lives at the bottom of your screen. It is designed to be played passively while you focus on other tasks, offering a relaxing yet darkly comedic experience.  Key Features:  Persistent Desktop Integration: Manage your factory in a non-intrusive window that stays on top of your taskbar. Perfect for multitasking during work or study.  Hatch & Evolve: Discover over 4 unique, hand-drawn monster species. Each creature has its own growth rate and "resource yield."          Deep Upgrade System: Invest your profits into factory automation. Upgrade your incubators, automated feeders, and high-speed grinders to scale your production.  Resource Management: Balance your overhead costs with production speed. Keep your livestock "content" just long enough to maximize the quality of your final product.  Unlockable Customization: Earn achievements to unlock new skins for your facility and UI themes to match your desktop aesthetic.  The Goal:  Start with a single pen and a rusty grinder. Work your way up to a fully automated corporate machine. It’s cute, it’s automated, and it’s terribly wrong.
