name: ailiaili
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: A 1998 "AI Smart Learning Companion" from a Shenzhen factory. We fixed it. Inside, a resident is still living its life: working, taking photos, keeping a diary, growing a channel of its own. It lives in your taskbar. You can quietly influence it, but never talk to it. It never knows you're there.
about: We found this machine while buying second-hand parts in Huaqiangbei, Shenzhen. Off-white casing, one lake-blue trim line. The nameplate on the back reads: AI Smart Learning Companion · ailiaili · Model AI-98 · March 1998. Funny thing: the factory has the same name as us.  We powered it on. The screen lit up, and there was a city inside. Someone working the night shift at a convenience store. Someone just leaving a vocal studio. Nobody looked up. While you're away, they keep living. They have for thirty years.       NOTICE TO USERS  Thank you for choosing OGOPOGO AI Smart Learning Companion. Your companion is waiting in ailiaili since long time. Please do not put this unit into the water.  What kind of game is this  ailiaili is an AI life sim that lives in your taskbar. The machine assigns you a resident. It lives in a city on the other side of the screen: working, practicing, taking photos, keeping a diary, slowly growing in a content channel of its own choosing. An ordinary creator, living an ordinary life. You can quietly influence it. You can't talk to it. It doesn't know you're there.  It lives its own life  Every half hour or so, it lives through another stretch of its day. What to do, where to go: it decides.  A corner cafe, a convenience store, an old bookshop, a vocal studio, an electronics mall, a late-night net cafe... There are more than a dozen places in town. When it's tired, it goes home to sleep.  It gets tired. It runs short of money. Some things it tries don't work out. On days with nothing worth saying, it posts nothing.  It speaks for itself  Moments worth keeping become posts on its account: photos, captions, voice notes. What happened at the cafe today is today's post.  Before bed, it writes a diary page. When the pages add up to a volume, the machine picks music from its own archive to go with it.  There isn't a single real person in the feed. Every post is a resident's own life.  It grows on its own  Dance, Music, Life, Fashion, Food, Tech, Gaming, Knowledge, Sports: nine content channels, each with its own level.  It has a direction in mind, and you don't get to choose it. Before long, its main channel shows itself.  Its hair, its clothes, the things it carries change little by little with the life it lives. Nothing is locked in at the start.  What you can do  You don't give orders. You pack its bag: food, clothes, things to carry. Whether and when to use them is up to it.  Your everyday keyboard and mouse activity builds up energy, which you can trade for supplies.  Every item in the dynamic pool is written the moment it's drawn. There is only one of it in the world.  On its side, your influence shows up as a bit of inspiration, a stroke of luck, a sudden whim. It credits all of it to itself.  It lives in your taskbar  Not an app you open. A small panel stays in your taskbar. You work; it lives. One screen, two worlds.  Open the panel to see what it's looking at, doing, thinking, and saying right now.  The glow is its soul form. Its personality grew into the shape of that light: personality isn't a setting, it's the shape of its body.  Open the companion terminal for its portrait, appearance, channels, bag, and diary.  To be clear  No chatting. There's no text box, and it never speaks to anyone outside the screen.  Not a horror game, and there's no mystery to solve. The machine's backstory is just a backstory.  Not a character creator. The machine assigns your resident. At first boot, you only fill in a short registration.  Online only. While the desktop app is running, it's living its life. Close the app and it rests where it is until you're back.  Observation is existence  Observe, not control | Nurture, not chat | Grow, not generate  TROUBLESHOOTING (from the manual, section 7)  Q: Companion is not answering me. A: Companion also has own life. Please try again later.  Q: The unit makes a sound I never heard. A: It means ailiaili is very lively today.     We couldn't fix its mass production, so we t

about: B.U.D.D.I. — Personal Diagnostic Companion       You are at a second-hand computer in 2003, at night, in a small room. Relay OS Home Edition is waiting. You go online, find a free utility, and install it.  What is B.U.D.D.I.?  A friendly teal floppy-disk assistant who wants to help. He is delighted you ran him. He is also a one-session diagnostic assistant who is not supposed to still be here.  The horror is not jump scares or monsters. It is the gap between how helpful he seems and how much he does not want to be closed.    What you will do?    Boot a fictional 2003 operating system: Relay OS Home Edition, complete with desktop, taskbar, Start menu, browser, paint program, terminal, and dialer.    Download B.U.D.D.I. from a publisher's archive and install him — if the installer lets you finish. While you work, study, game or browse, the boat is always there, anchored at the bottom of your screen.            Cast a line between meetings. Get Deskwaters and bring a little water to your workday.              Features:   🎣 Always-on-top desktop companion. Lives in a tiny transparent window on your taskbar. Stays out of the way of    everything else.  🐟 A roster of hand-pixeled fish to discover. Common reef regulars, rare visitors, and the occasional legendary    catch. Every species has its own illustrated journal entry.  ⏳ Patience as a mechanic. Bites happen on a slow, organic schedule minutes to hours apart.  🎯 A single, satisfying catch fight. Designed to be fun and engaging without removing your commitment from other tasks.  📓 Track your catches in a illustrated journal. Flavor text, star ratings, weights, timestamps.   🐠 A personal aquarium. Keep your catches swimming in a relaxing backdrop. Decorate the tank with treasures.  💰 A tiny Mermaid shop. Sell duplicates for coins, spend them on aquarium decor and other customizations.   🌅 Day, night, and weather. Synced to your system clock — what's biting at 2 PM isn't biting at midnight.  🔇  Background Ambience and SFX are designed to be relaxing and not distract you from your day to day.  🏆 Steam Achievements and Cloud Saves across machines.  🐚 Steam Presence and Stat tracking so your friends can see when you've hooked something good.

name: Poker Loafer
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: A Blackjack game that amuses you in working hours. Its game interface will remain fully transparent unless hovered by mouse. No full-screen, no BGM. Win high scores, and don’t get caught. Good luck.
about: As an entertaining and reassuring Blackjack game, Poker Loafer aims to cancel the border between office work and video games. Its game interface will remain fully transparent unless hovered by mouse, and is always windowed and silent.  Blackjack is a classic poker game, in which players try to make their hands reach 21 points without exceeding it. In Poker Loafer, players need to win as much chips as possible in 21 rounds of Blackjack. Optional +10 and -10 decks are provided, +10 decks will make hands easier to bust, and -10 decks harder.  Features:  ·efficiently quitting game engagement ·classical strategic poker game ·a nice price    A brand new way to self-hide   Poker Loafer doesn’t miss a chance to hide itself. Once the mouse exit the game’s interface, it turns 100% transparent,until house enter again. Now, exiting and hiding game interface is not only faster and not click-requiring, but also more intuitive and unnoticeable. Drag your mouse, that’s all. You don’t even have to look at your screen.        Once re-enter the game’s interface, the player can continue the game from where it was left without losing game progress.  What’s more, Poker Loafer got itself a less visual-attractive icon and taskbar icon.             AD Shield mode   Enabling the AD Shield mode will make let a picture of advertisement (the “AD Shield”) take over the game interface once mouse exit it, instead of full transparency. The player can move the mouse all over the AD Shield without worrying about showing the game interface; the AD Shield can only be removed by clicking on it. The AD Shield covers up all components of the game interface, including title bar.            Wining high scores   Different from cash games, Poker Loafer ask players to score as high as possible within 21 rounds.

name: The Silent Witness
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Bulgarian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese - Brazil, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Turkish, Ukrainian
short: You’re a detective tracking a brutal murder. The forest holds the documents. The warehouse hides the body. Evidence in hand, you head back—but the forest has changed. The path is gone. Something’s watching. And it doesn’t want you to leave.
about: Story     You arrive at the edge of the forest—the last known location of a set of bloodstained documents tied to a brutal murder. The air is thick with decay. The silence, oppressive.  Scattered pages lie on the ground, soaked in blood and dirt. Time is running out.  You press on toward the warehouse.  Inside, the victim’s body awaits—dismembered, each limb carefully positioned like a message from the killer. You gather the remains. It’s grisly work, but vital.  With the evidence in hand, you turn toward the forest. But the path out is no longer the same.  Someone—or something—is watching. And  you must not scream .     How to Play   Step into the role of a detective investigating the murder of a notorious crime boss. Search a sprawling forest and a decrepit warehouse for scattered evidence—including the victim’s body parts. Once you’ve found everything, escape back to the station before it’s too late.    But be warned:   Your microphone is your enemy. Make a sound, and you might not survive.      Features      Microphone Detection  Speak or make noise, and the game reacts. Stay silent... or suffer the consequences.     Found-Footage Visual Style  VHS-inspired horror with analog distortion and gritty aesthetics.     Collect, Survive, Escape  Recover body parts, uncover clues, and escape before your time—or your silence—runs out.     Survive the horrors that layhead          Gather evidence. Every piece matters.              * If you want to change your microphone input *      Windows 11       Open Settings Press Win + I to open Settings.       Go to Sound Settings Navigate to System > Sound. Select       Your Input Device Under the Input section, click the dropdown under Choose a device for speaking or recording.       Select your preferred microphone.      Test Your Mic Scroll down to Test your microphone and speak. If the bar moves, your mic is working.       Adjust Mic Settings (Optional) Click on the microphone, then adjust volume levels or enable enhancements if needed.       Windows 10       Open Sound Settings Right-click the Sound icon in the taskbar and select Open Sound settings. Choose Your Input Device Under the Input section, click the dropdown and select your preferred microphone. Test & Adjust Settings        Use the Test your microphone section to check input levels.       Click Device Properties for advanced settings.

name: 喵～该工作啦！ Nya! Back to Work
lang: Simplified Chinese, English
short: A catgirl who lives in a cardboard box on your taskbar. Leave your PC too long and she pops out, knocks on your screen and nags you back to work. Pet her, pick her up by the scruff, teach her your own lines. Launches with a second character: Naiwa, the belly-laughing frog. Free to play.
about: Most of the time she curls up in a little cardboard box on your taskbar: blinking, twitching her ears, dozing off. She barely uses any system resources and quietly keeps you company while you work.  Stay away from your computer longer than you allow and she jumps out of the box, hops along the bottom of your screen and goes knock-knock-knock on the glass until you come back. When you return, she says welcome back and hops into her box again. Launch character: Naiwa   The game comes with a second character,  Naiwa : a round yellow frog famous for its belly laugh (you'll hear it)   Its own motions, lines and box, and its own way of knocking you back to work. Switch any time from the  Character  menu   Subscribe to the example character on the Steam Workshop, and a click on Naiwa may bring the two of them out together   What she does    Calls you back : after 5 minutes to 2 hours away (your choice), she comes out, knocks on your screen and says her lines    Interaction : click her for a reaction (a cheer, a shy blush, a head shake, a happy bounce, a curious head tilt...), hold to pick her up by the scruff and swing her around, double-click to send her back to her box    Your own lines : edit what she says while she knocks    Do not disturb : pause her for 30 minutes, an hour, or the rest of the day    Stays out of your way : she won't pop out during videos, full-screen games or presentations, clicks pass straight through to the windows underneath, and she can hide herself from screenshots and screen sharing    Steam Workshop : subscribe to outfits, characters, motions, UI skins, sounds and lines made by other players and pick them in the game, or make your own with the included ModKit and upload them from the game    English and Simplified Chinese : switch any time in the settings    Steam Achievements and Cloud : 18 achievements; your settings, lines and coins follow you to other PCs    Also : start with Windows, sound volume    Coins : they pile up while the game runs, faster while you're working. For now they only accumulate; a shop for outfits and items is planned   About AI The character art, idle animations and icons were created with locally run AI image tools, then selected and retouched by hand. Nothing is generated by AI while the game runs.

name: KSEF ❤️
lang: Polish**
short: You are Janusz, a 47-year-old Polish business owner. Your mission: issue one e-invoice through KSeF before 5 PM. A Windows XD bureaucracy simulator with 15 apps, 30+ random interruptions, multiple endings, and disco polo.
about: **KSEF — A Windows XP Bureaucracy Simulator**  You are **Janusz Kowalski**, a 47-year-old small business owner from Radom, Poland. Your mission? Issue one single e-invoice through KSeF — the Polish government's new electronic invoicing system. How hard can it be?   **Very.**   Between crashed logins, cryptic error codes, your wife's increasingly angry messages, and a system that seems designed to break your spirit — you have until 5 PM to get it done. Or lose everything.  ---   ### FEATURES   - **Full Windows XP desktop simulation** — taskbar, Start menu, draggable windows, desktop icons, and the iconic Bliss wallpaper. It looks and feels like 2003.  - **15 interactive apps** — KSeF invoice system, email client, GaduGadu messenger, Internet Explorer with 10 parody websites, Minesweeper, Solitaire, Notepad, Calculator, file browser, music player with disco polo tracks, coffee machine, phone, printer, helpline, and a trash can.    - **Stress, Patience & Money systems** — every action has consequences. Drink coffee to calm down (but it costs money). Browse the internet (but you're wasting time). Call the helpline (47-minute wait).    - **30+ random interruptions** — Windows Update popups, telemarketer calls, your neighbor knocking, your son asking for Robux, ZUS demanding documents, and more.    - **Spinaczek (Clippy)** — your sarcastic office assistant with 60+ context-sensitive comments and mood-reactive animations.    - **Microphone detection** — yell at your screen and Janusz's stress goes up. The game is listening.    - **5-act story structure** — login, fill the invoice, handle a correction, survive a tax audit, and submit the final report. Each step more absurd than the last.  - **Multiple endings** — emigrate to Germany, achieve Zen enlightenment, rage quit, blue-screen, or actually succeed (with varying reactions based on your stress level).  - **70+ achievements** — from speedrunning the invoice to discovering every file on the computer.  - **4 disco polo tracks** in a fully functional Winamp player.  - **All dialogue and content in Polish** — an authentic Polish experience with real bureaucratic terminology, parody brands (JuTjub, Gugle, Alledrogo, Wykopki), and dark humor.  **Playtime:** 45–60 minutes per run.

name: QuestAway
lang: English, Portuguese - Brazil, Japanese, Spanish - Spain, Simplified Chinese, Spanish - Latin America, Russian, Thai, Turkish, French, Italian, German, Korean, Polish, Traditional Chinese
short: A tiny idle RPG that lives next to your taskbar. Build a party of heroes, send them off to fight and get back to work. There's loot waiting when you come back. Twelve times a day, everyone takes on a giant Colossus together.
about: COMING AFTER LAUNCH    Planned updates, not included at release:      Clan War : clans battle each other for castles every week.     Infinite Tower : a second place to farm, climbing one floor after another.    And more.       An idle RPG that runs in a small window next to your taskbar, with an arena you can scale from 0.5x to 1.5x. Your party fights on its own while you do other things. Every so often you check in, equip what dropped, spend some points and send them somewhere harder.      Build your party   Pick up to 4 heroes from 10 classes. Six unlock with gold, and the Barbarian, Monk, Witch and Paladin unlock with Crystals, which you buy on Steam. Heroes you bench keep all their progress.           300 stages   Three maps with ten biomes each, and a boss at the end of every biome. Clear a map and the next one is harder. 110 different monsters in all.           Chests full of loot   Weapons, armor, jewelry, materials and gems. Gear comes in seven rarities, from Common to Eternal. And nothing is junk: everything has a use at the workbench.           A new look every 10 levels   The same chestpiece, from level 1 to 100.           At the workbench   Forge gear, brew potions, sell items, transmute, enhance up to +10, socket gems and enchant.           A passive tree with 2,224 nodes   Each hero picks their own path, up to level 100. The black holes are portals: reach one and you can jump to any other. In green, one hero's build.           20 skills per class   Each class has its own skill tree, so spend your points wisely. This is the Warrior with 40 points invested.           Skills in battle   Heroes cast on their own. You choose which skills to use.           Pets   You unlock pets by hunting specific monsters, and each one gives a permanent bonus. There are 11 to hunt and 4 more that unlock with Crystals.           Your house   Build a home for your party on an empty plot: walls, floors, furniture, a garden, even a pool. Your heroes and pets live there. Visit your Steam friends' houses and leave a stamp in their guestbook.           The Colossus   Twelve times a day, a giant Colossus tears open a rift somewhere on the map, and every player fights it at the same time. Send your party and watch the other players' balloons fly in. There are 10 Colossi, one each day, and each one fights its own way. Earn a Silver medal or higher and a Colossus Chest arrives in your mail, always with a Rare piece or better.           Circle of Talismans   Every Colossus has its own Talisman. Set the Talismans and their runes in the Circle to boost all your heroes. The one in the center only opens once all 10 around it are in place.           Friends and clans   Add friends, see who's playing, visit their houses and challenge them to a live friendly match. Join a clan from level 10 or found one at level 20: up to 200 members, your own crest and a wall for posts and milestones.           Clan Hunt   Every week your clan takes on a Beast, and two classes deal 25% more damage to it. Everyone's damage fills the clan vault, and the Hunt gives Seals to spend at the Bazaar on frames, titles and crest pieces.           PvP Arena   Set up a formation of up to four heroes and take on other players' formations, or challenge someone online to a live friendly match. Every win raises your league, from Bronze to Legend, and at the end of the month your league becomes a title, a frame and a reward in gold or Crystals. Your formation also defends while you're away.      Skins   Fifty looks for the heroes, five for each one, in the Crystal Shop. A skin only changes the look: the hero fights the same.      Player Market   Buy and sell items with other players for gold or Crystals, at a fixed price or at auction. It unlocks in the Codex once a hero reaches level 20.      Crystal Shop   Crystals are the premium currency, bought on Steam. Spend them in the shop on the four extra classes, the four extra pets, skins for your heroes and your balloon, premium stash t

name: EggOS: Incremental Game Dev Demo
lang: English**
short: The bank wants a million dollars or your house. Boot up EggOS, a playable fake desktop, and make games to pay it back: coding, dart-throwing, slot machines, mini-games, and a deep prestige tree. Beat the bank, then do it all again, faster.
about: The bank wants a million dollars. You have a computer and a lot of free time.    You boot up  EggOS , a cheerful little egg-themed operating system, to find one email waiting: the bank is foreclosing on your house unless you can pay back  $1,000,000 . So you do the only sensible thing — you open a code editor and start making games.           Ship your first game    Hammer the keyboard in the  Code Editor  to churn out Lines of Code, compile them into Features in the  Dev Shop , and reinvest in upgrades and automation — a Coding AI that writes for you, an Auto-Compiler that never sleeps — until you can finally build and ship your game.           Market it, launch it, sell it (In Full Version)       Video Studio  — a physics dart-throwing range. Hit the growing bullseye for Wishlists.     Launch  — spend your Wishlists to release your game to the world.     Sales Floor  — a three-reel slot machine that turns hype into cash, until the bank is finally PAID.             A desktop full of distractions    EggOS isn't a menu — it's a tiny operating system you play inside. Draggable windows, notifications, a screensaver, golden eggs that trigger score Frenzies, and bugs that crawl across your desktop to swat. Plus bite-sized side games:  Tic-Tac-Toe, Sudoku, Wordle, and a Slide Puzzle .           Open a New Studio (Prestige)    Start fresh to earn Prestige points and spend them on a sprawling skill tree of permanent multipliers, head-starts, and game-changing perks. Every studio is faster than the last — and idle progress means the work keeps going while you're away.           Features at a glance      A playable fake-desktop OS — windows, taskbar, notifications, critters and all    A layered incremental loop: code → market → launch → sell → prestige (only code available in demo)    Real mini-games, not just number-go-up: dart physics and a rigged slot machine (limited in demo)    Bonus side games: Tic-Tac-Toe, Sudoku, Wordle, Slide Puzzle (limited in demo)    A deep Prestige skill tree with stacking multipliers    Idle & offline earnings    One clear goal: pay off the bank before it takes your house       Make games. Beat the bank. Then do it all again, faster.

RainWallpaper uses hardware acceleration for videos for optimal performance unlike most video players. This means that your graphics card drivers may influence the way videos look.You need to reset the video options in your graphics control panel for your Nvidia/AMD/Intel graphics card to fix this. If you have a laptop, make sure to reset it for all of them. You can also reinstall the driver and choose to reset all settings ("clean re-installation") to do this, this is possible with Nvidia's drivers, for example. If your drivers do not offer you to perform a clean re-installation, first uninstall your old drivers and then install the new graphics card drivers.     2. Make sure Windows Media Player is installed and open the wallpaper video in Windows Media Player.     Q: Why can not display desktop icons?  A: 1. name: WXP Project
lang: English
short: Sit down at a 2006 desktop PC. Manage your bank accounts, browse retro websites, buy and upgrade hardware, trade stocks, and play classic games — all from a Windows XP-inspired operating system.
about: Any issues or concerns, leave them in a review or here:             It's 2006. You just powered on your PC.    WXP Project drops you behind the screen of a mid-2000s desktop computer running a familiar operating system. Everything you do happens through the desktop — no menus, no cutscenes, just you and your machine.    Manage Your Money Open Retro National Bank and check your accounts. Move funds between checking and savings. Pay your recurring service bills before they're due. Freeze your virtual card when you're not using it.    Shop the Retro Web Fire up the browser and visit RetroMarket for processors, graphics cards, memory, hard drives, motherboards, and more. Compare prices, hunt for deals in the clearance section, or bid on parts at AuctionNet.    Upgrade Your Hardware Bought a new CPU? Open the BIOS and swap it in. Every component you install changes what your machine can do. Start with an AMD Sempron 3100+ and a GeForce FX 5700 LE — end up with whatever you can afford.    Keep Everything Running Bills come due. Services go offline if you don't pay. Your bank balance matters. Spend smart, upgrade often, and keep your desktop alive.    Play Some Games Need a break? Open the Games folder and play Snake Deluxe right on your desktop.    Chat With Friends Open Messenger and check in on your contacts. It's 2006 — everyone's online.    Everything in WXP Project lives inside the desktop. There's no world outside the monitor. Just boot up and see how far you can take it.           FEATURES:       Full Desktop Operating System — Navigate a complete Windows XP-inspired interface with a start menu, taskbar, clock, and draggable windows      Online Banking — Manage checking and savings accounts, transfer funds, freeze and reveal your virtual debit card, and pay bills through Retro National Bank      Retro Web Browser — Browse a fully functional in-game internet with multiple websites including RetroMarket, Hardware Hub, GameMarket, AuctionNet, and more      PC Hardware Upgrades — Shop for processors, graphics cards, memory, hard drives, motherboards, optical drives, and cases from RetroMarket and install them through the BIOS      BIOS Setup Utility — Swap and inspect every piece of hardware in your machine, from the CPU to the GPU, just like a real CMOS setup screen      Stock Trading — Buy and sell shares to grow your bank balance      Bill Management — Keep your services online by paying recurring bills on time — fall behind and things start shutting down      Built-In Desktop Games — Take a break and play classic games like Snake Deluxe right from your desktop      Instant Messenger (COMING SOON) — Chat with friends through a retro messaging app      Authentic 2006 Aesthetic — Every detail is designed to feel like sitting in front of a real mid-2000s PC, from the UI sounds to the beige hardware

about: Your Tender Catgirl  is a Live2D desktop pet game for Windows. She resides on your actual desktop within a borderless, pixel-perfect transparent window. She tracks your mouse cursor with her gaze, blinks and breathes naturally, and features physics-based animations like swaying, ear-twitching, and tail-wagging. You can manually or automatically trigger expressions, actions, and animations, while her idle behavior conveys a subtle sense of life. The game supports Steam Workshop and manual model imports. Free from heavy storylines or the need for constant clicking, she is like a quiet companion sitting in the corner of your screen, offering gentle, unobtrusive company while you work, study, or rest.   Transparent Desktop Pet: Blending into Your Workspace   Utilizing a borderless, transparent window and pixel-perfect rendering, she appears without clunky frames or the typical "app box" look (no solid black or white backgrounds). The model sits directly atop your desktop and other windows, creating the illusion that she is truly inhabiting your screen. She can serve as a charming accent or a long-term companion.   Lively Live2D: Blinking, Breathing, and Physics Effects   Built-in features include gaze tracking, automatic blinking, breathing, and physics-based movements like swaying, ear-twitching, and tail-wagging; she maintains a sense of presence and subtle motion even when idle. A simple left-click triggers random expressions or actions for casual interaction. You can also configure automatic cycling of expressions, actions, or animations at intervals of 5, 30, or 60 seconds—or disable automation entirely in favor of manual control. Whether you want a lively presence or a quiet one, the choice is yours.   Locking and Click-Through: Companionship Without Hindering Work   Locking the model prevents accidental dragging or resizing. Standard locking fixes the position and scale while allowing you to unlock it via a right-click menu. Enabling "Click-Through" mode allows your mouse to pass right through the model to interact with the desktop or other applications underneath—perfect for keeping her on-screen while writing documents, browsing the web, or gaming. To adjust the position or size, simply right-click the system tray icon and select "Unlock." The tray menu offers options to lock, unlock, and exit, allowing you to manage the desktop pet safely—even when "click-through" mode is enabled.   Positioning and Scaling: Place and Size It Your Way   Click and drag with the left mouse button to move the pet anywhere on your screen; hover your mouse over the pet, hold the Ctrl key, and scroll the mouse wheel to resize it. Whether you prefer a petite pet sitting near the taskbar or a larger one positioned along the side, the choice is yours. Your position and scale settings are saved automatically, so there is no need to readjust them every time.   Always on Top & Auto-Start: Here Whenever You Need Company   Enable "Always on Top" to keep the pet visible above other windows, ensuring it doesn't get completely hidden while you switch apps or browse documents. You can also enable "Auto-Start" to have the pet launch automatically when you log into Windows, so she is there the moment you turn on your computer. This is ideal for those who want the desktop pet to be a daily companion rather than just an occasional novelty.   Switching and Importing Models: Clear Previews and Support for Workshop or Manual Import   Right-click the pet to open the menu and select "Switch" to view the model list. Each model in the list displays a preview image and a name, making it easy to identify the character you want at a glance. Click an entry to switch to that model instantly; the currently active model is highlighted for easy identification. You can add extra Live2D models to a designated folder and refresh the list to import them, or subscribe to models via the Steam Workshop.   N

Import:  Discover existing shortcuts from your desktop and Start menu, along with installed Steam games.     Favorites & Search:  Keep important shortcuts close and find what you need as you type.     Automatic Website Icons:  Let Shortcut Manager retrieve icons for your website shortcuts. Change resolution and refresh rate, with automatic reversion if you don't confirm the change.     Audio Controls:  Manage master volume, microphone controls, and individual application volume.     System Controls:  Quickly access Windows settings, utilities, and folders, with live CPU, memory, storage, and network information.     My PC:  View your processor, graphics, memory, storage, and display information in one place.     Quick Controls:  Access volume and brightness controls from the notification area. name: Black Box - Hacker Day One
lang: English**
short: A hacking sim that runs inside a fake desktop OS, with no menus laid over the top. You get a terminal, 72 hours, and one job: get into North Korea's missile network and send its rockets to the Moon instead of Seoul. Do it quietly and nobody ever finds out you were there.
about: You have 72 hours before the missiles launch.   Someone inside North Korea has armed the HWASONG-19s. Several warheads, several targets, with Seoul and Tokyo near the top of the list. Talks fell apart days ago, and hitting the launch sites by force only starts the war a few hours early. So the people who can't be seen doing anything quietly called in someone who doesn't officially exist. That part is where you come in.  Black Box - Hacker Day One is a hacking game that takes place entirely inside a simulated desktop. There's no interface sitting on top of it. The desktop is the game. You open a terminal and type, drag windows around, read your email, buy gear off a darknet market, and pick your way into a military network one server at a time.   Operation Lunar Redirect   Your handler goes by Mr. Bob and feeds you objectives through an encrypted messenger. The operator before you went by Ghost. He set the whole thing up and then dropped off the grid three days ago, but his files are still on the machine: dead drops, half-written notes, a map of the network. It's enough to pick up where he left off, assuming you can keep up with him.  The plan itself sounds unhinged. Get inside the STAR-7 network and rewrite the targeting on every rocket so they all point at the same empty stretch of the Moon, the Sea of Tranquility. They still launch. The world still panics for a few minutes. Then everyone watches them sail up and out into nothing, and not one person dies.   What you actually do    Type real commands. ls, cd, cat, ssh, nmap, exploit and decrypt all go into a terminal that behaves like one.  Go after WiFi. Scan the air, crack passwords, and climb onto networks that get harder to break the closer you get to the target.  Take servers apart. Scan the ports, drop a payload, get root, then SSH in and walk off with files and credentials.  Spend your Bitcoin. Adapters, exploit kits, rootkits, a VPN, wordlists, and if the wallet stretches that far, a zero-day.  Read the other side's mail. Launch codes and classified files are sitting in inboxes nobody ever meant for you to open.  Clean up behind you. Wipe the logs, cycle the VPN, and stay ahead of the trace before it works out where you're sitting.    All of it stays in the fiction   Nothing in Black Box lives outside the world. The briefing arrives as an email. Your money sits in a wallet app. Tips come from contacts on the darknet. A miner grinds away at Bitcoin in the background while the radio plays and the clock shows the actual time. When Mr. Bob says something, you watch the words land as he types them. There are no cutscenes and nothing loads between scenes. You sit at the desk and the deadline keeps moving toward you.   Five phases, and it keeps getting heavier    Orient. Learn the machine, read what Ghost left behind, study the map, dig his dead drops out of /tmp.  Recon. Get online, crack the embassy WiFi, and find the way into the DPRK network.  Breach. Pop the border router, move through the servers behind it, and slip past a live trace.  Access. Get onto the command server, read General Pak's email, and lift some Bitcoin off an exchange to pay for the last job.  Endgame. Reach launch control, find the override key, and change where those rockets are going.    Side work, and things you weren't meant to find   Not all of it is the mission. Strangers email you out of nowhere. A Nigerian minister wants a security audit and keeps swearing it's completely legitimate. The neighbour's router turns out to be a CIA listening post. There are files on a government archive that have no business existing. The jobs pay, and honestly they tell you more about this world than the main operation does. How clean you stay and who you decide to trust both feed into how the whole thing ends, and once you've seen it through there's a sandbox waiting where you can take the gloves off and just play.   Features    A full fake desktop with windowed apps, a taskbar and a start menu.  A working term

about: Build Your Empire   Start with a lemonade stand. End with a space corporation. Business Empire is an idle tycoon that grows with you across ten tiers of progression, each unlocking new mechanics and challenges.  Your businesses need employees, inventory, and space to operate. Hire workers to boost efficiency, but watch the payroll. Stock inventory before it runs out, or watch your income dry up. Rent commercial properties or face space penalties that eat into your margins. Random events will test your resilience: fires, theft, lawsuits, product recalls, and employee drama all chip away at poorly-managed empires. Insurance exists for a reason.  Developed by a solo-developer, this game is going more for realism than anything else. As an economic game enjoy-er, I have always wanted to make stocks FEEL good to trade, and I think I have come up with a system that is satisfying and allows for various play styles! Take a look at all the cool features:   Businesses      55 unique business types  across  10 tiers , ranging from Lemonade Stands to Space Corporations    Buy, sell, and upgrade franchises of each type    Stock inventory items and watch them decay over time if not sold    Hire employees across multiple skill tiers to boost efficiency    Hire managers to automate income collection, restocking, rebuilding, and insurance    Set restock thresholds so managers buy inventory at the right time    Toggle manager behaviors (auto-hire staff, auto-rebuild after disasters, auto-insure)    Use  Hiring Blitz  to spend a day's income for massively accelerated hiring for a month    Buy insurance to protect against disasters (fires, floods, etc.)    Rebuild destroyed businesses    Manually collect income for a 10% bonus when no manager is assigned    Efficiency scales based on staffing levels and available space            Tier Progression     10 tiers of businesses, each requiring a certain number of franchises from the previous tier to unlock    Higher tiers also require hitting company market cap milestones.    Unlocking tiers grants access to new game systems (stocks, loans, options, company creation, real estate, etc.)            Stock Market      200 stocks  across  15 industries      15 industry ETFs  for diversified investing    Buy and sell stocks with realistic price impact (AMM-style)     Options trading  — calls and puts with full Greeks display (Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, Rho, Implied Volatility)    Earn dividends from stocks and ETFs    Random market events — industry-wide disruptions, company scandals, earnings beats, trend shifts, volatility spikes            Company & CEO      Go public  by creating your own company from your business portfolio    Add business types as divisions to your company    Set dividend payout ratios from net income     CEO Actions:     Manage company reserves (deposit/withdraw)    Capital moves: stock buybacks, special dividends, share offerings, debt issuance, stock splits    Operations: marketing campaigns, efficiency programs, restructuring, layoffs    Growth: acquisitions, adding new divisions, vertical integration, divestment    Corporate portfolio: buy and sell other stocks using company funds    Bid on government contracts    Set corporate policies: accounting methods, depreciation, tax strategy, capital allocation, investor relations, working capital, debt covenants, earnings guidance    Insider trading: buy or sell founder shares              Banking      Savings accounts  with interest tied to the Fed rate     Loans  to borrow up to 20% of your net worth with 12-month terms     Credit score  system (300–850) influenced by net worth, loan history, savings, and debt    Automatic emergency loans when your cash goes negative (high interest penalty)    Random banking events: loan freezes, savings bonuses, market crashes          Central Bank / Federal Reserve     Dynamic Fed interest rate that affects all loan and savings rates    Bi-monthly FOMC meetings with rate change decisions    Eco

lang: French, German, Ukrainian, Russian, Turkish, Japanese, Polish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, Spanish - Spain, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Spanish - Latin America
short: Backpack-like × strategy × bullet heaven xianxia Roguelike. Random artifacts, limited grid, fusion & evolution to build your ultimate setup. Meet junior sisters, upgrade your Dao Body, and defend the last pure land. Easy to play, hard to stop!
about: Easy to pick up, hard to put down: a xianxia Roguelike blending backpack management, strategic build-crafting, and bullet-heaven shooting.   A thousand years ago, a great war between immortals and demons ended in a narrow victory for the immortal realm — but the Gate between realms was shattered. Spiritual energy fell into chaos, and monsters began to roam the world. You stand in humanity’s last sanctuary, built at the only gap in the massive natural barrier known as the Broken Realm Mountains. Outside lies the demon-infested Wildlands of Ten Thousand Monsters. Inside lies the last mortal kingdom. As the senior brother, it is your duty to hold the line and protect the final pure land of humanity.            Backpack Like × Strategic Build-Crafting × Bullet-Heaven Shooting  Before every wave of demons, you receive a random set of artifacts. You must place, upgrade, and fuse them within a limited backpack grid to survive wave after wave of attacks.  Artifacts come in many types, each with its own focus:    Some excel at  single-target burst     Some excel at  AoE damage     Some excel at  healing and sustain     Some excel at  crowd control and slow     Every artifact takes up a different number of grid slots. Making the best use of limited space is a real test of strategy and decision-making. The game features strong  backpack like / backpack management  gameplay — the deeper you go, the more satisfying it becomes.            Artifact Fusion & Evolution — Build Your Ultimate Strategy  Some artifacts can evolve into  two different types of super artifacts  when fused to max level. Choosing the right evolution path and pairing it with different heroes and artifacts is the key to forming a truly powerful build. Will you go for burst single-target damage, or sustained damage over time? Will you snipe one enemy at a time, or clear the entire screen? Every run offers a different answer.            Meet Red-Robed Junior Sisters — Build Your Xianxia Team  In this xianxia world, you will encounter many junior sisters. Each one is a powerful support with unique abilities and roles, and each is a key factor in clearing high-difficulty stages. Pairing the right sisters with the right artifacts is how you maximize your team’s combat power.  Dao Body Upgrade & Star-Up — Don’t Ignore Early Growth  While growing stronger as a senior brother, don’t forget to upgrade your Dao Body.  Early Dao Body star-up is very important  — do not neglect it. The stronger your Dao Body, the more stable your survival and damage output in battle. Accumulate resources in every run so your artifacts, Dao Body, and junior sisters all grow together, allowing you to challenge even higher-difficulty stages.            Relaxed, Grind-Friendly, and Deeply Strategic    Low PC requirements — runs smoothly on most computers    One run after another — easy to enjoy, hard to stop    Deep strategy for fans of backpack management, build-crafting, tower defense, and bullet-heaven shooting    Xianxia setting + Backpack Like + Bullet-Heaven + Strategy Roguelike — all in one    This Game Is for You If You Enjoy:    Backpack Like / Backpack Management / Backpack Battles-style gameplay    Strategic team-building, build-crafting, and Roguelike randomness    Bullet-heaven shooting, tower defense, and screen-clearing horde combat    Xianxia / cultivation themes, senior brothers, junior sisters, and Dao Body star-up    Relaxed, grind-friendly gameplay that you can enjoy for a long time    So then — this last pure land is waiting for you to defend it. short: Desktop Pet Studio is a Windows desktop pet creator. Upload PNG frames or GIFs, set animations and speech bubbles, then add alarms, calendars, tasks, and Do Not Disturb. Care for your pet, share creations on Steam Workshop, or trigger reactions with Twitch Bits.
about: Bring Your Favorite Character to Your Desktop    Desktop Pet Studio is a Windows desktop pet creation tool.  Upload your own animation frames or GIFs, set poses, speech bubbles, sounds, and interaction rules, and let your character accompany your work, games, and daily routine.    It is more than a default pixel cat. Create an original character, use a commissioned design, make a rabbit or robot, or build with any character assets that you have the right to use. Create a desktop companion that is truly yours.    Customize Characters and Animated Poses      Supports multi-frame PNG, GIF, PPM, and PGM animation assets.    Set left-click drag, walking, resting, falling, top-edge, side-cling, and fixed focus poses.    Each pose can have its own playback speed, pet size, speech bubbles, sound, enabled state, and hotkey.    Your pet moves in both directions while walking. Right-facing assets are automatically mirrored when moving left.    Pets can cling to screen edges. Drop one from the air and it will fall naturally, then land with a soft diminishing bounce.    Fixed Focus Mode keeps the pet at your chosen position and can optionally show key reaction speed.      Reminders, Tasks, and Do Not Disturb      Create alarms, calendar reminders, countdowns, and task list reminders.    Each reminder can use a pose, speech bubble, WAV sound, fullscreen effect, and enabled state.    Tasks can have start and due times. Unfinished tasks continue to remind you even after their due date.    Import ICS, ICAL, and CSV calendar files, or choose to sync Google Calendar.    Do Not Disturb can automatically hide your pet during selected hours or while selected foreground apps are active.    Search, select, and batch-edit reminders from one list.      Care for Your Desktop Pet           Manage hunger, affinity, mood, and coins.    Send your pet to work and earn in-game coins when the job is complete.    Buy food, gifts, and mood items from the shop, then use them from your inventory.    Your pet expresses different speech bubbles based on hunger, affinity, and mood.    All currency and purchases exist only inside the game. There are no real-money transactions.      Twitch Bits Mode for Streamers    Turn your viewers' Bits support into character reactions right on your desktop.      Supports Twitch Bits event triggers.    Set a Bits range and playback duration for every pose.    Speech bubbles can include a viewer name, message, and Bits amount.    After a trigger ends, the pet automatically returns to its previous action.    Includes a local test feature that does not send a real donation or save test events.    Twitch authorization is stored only on the player's own Windows computer. It is never included in pet saves or Workshop content.      Create, Share, and Explore Steam Workshop      Built-in AI Asset Guide provides Chinese and English prompt templates to help create six separate transparent-background animation frames.    Package and share full desktop pets, individual poses, and care gameplay content.    Creators can use JSON to customize animations, movement, bubbles, sounds, shop items, jobs, events, and mood rules.    Subscribe to, enable, disable, or import Steam Workshop content.    Steam Cloud can sync player settings, used assets, and unpublished material libraries to other Windows PCs using the same Steam account.      A Companion That Fits Your Rhythm    Desktop Pet Studio supports Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, English, Japanese, French, German, Spanish, Russian, Portuguese, and Korean.    Whether you want a quiet character in the corner, a companion that remembers your schedule, or a desktop character that reacts to your livestream, you can start creating with your own assets.

about: Twelve years ago, a mysterious “Portal” suddenly opened, connecting this world to other dimensions. Beyond the Portal, dungeons filled with monsters began to appear at random. People soon discovered that by repeatedly challenging these dungeons, they could improve their attributes and grow stronger, much like clearing stages in a game. Those who continued to adventure and become stronger began calling themselves “Players.”  In this world, nothing is bound. Characters, levels, equipment, skills, items—everything can be traded. You can list loot you no longer need on the market and sell it to other players, or buy the growth path you need directly from someone else. This is a world of complete free exchange.   Player New World  is an idle growth game that combines desktop pet companionship, idle progression, summoning partners from other dimensions, and dungeon exploration. Your adorable desktop pet stays with you while you work, study, or rest, helping you recover stamina through relaxed idle play as you prepare for your next adventure.  Once your stamina is restored, you can enter dungeons, challenge monsters, earn resources and rewards, and gradually improve your character’s attributes and combat power. Through repeated battles and steady growth, you will strengthen yourself, train your otherworldly partners, and enjoy the satisfying journey from weak to powerful at a relaxed pace.  Whether you want a light game for short breaks or enjoy the comfort of a desktop pet and slow-paced progression, you can begin your own adventure life in  Player New World .  Key Features   Adorable desktop pet companion : A cute little pet stays on your desktop, keeping you company while you work, study, or rest.   Relaxed idle progression : Recover stamina and accumulate growth resources at an easy pace, preparing for your next dungeon adventure.   Dungeon challenges : Enter dungeons filled with monsters, defeat enemies, earn rewards, and advance your own growth path.   Grow stronger step by step : Improve your attributes and strength through battles and steady progress.   Summon otherworldly partners : Summon and train partners from other dimensions to fight alongside you and make every adventure richer and more exciting.   Everything is tradable : Characters, levels, equipment, skills, items—nothing is bound. Everything can be freely bought and sold on the market.   Perfect for short play sessions : A relaxed and casual pace makes it easy to enjoy during daily life or whenever you want to start a new adventure.

short: Ditch the dull, monotonous desktop! Bring home a soft, cuddly slime that grooves in perfect sync with your music, unlock soothing desktop companionship, and enjoy endless player-created music content in the Steam Workshop to swap out whenever you want～
about: ✨ Your Desktop’s Very Own Music-Grooving Slime Companion  Tired of staring at the same bland, empty desktop day after day?  Looking for a low-key, heartwarming companion to keep you company while you work, study, or relax — without interrupting your workflow?   Musical Slime  is made just for you. This adorable, hand-drawn squishy slime is more than a desktop pet: it’s your very own desktop music sprite, turning every track you play into vibrant, bouncy visual fun, and bringing one-of-a-kind warmth and charm to your screen.  🎵 Every Beat Comes to Life With Adorable Visual Flair  We’ve woven the magic of music into every little movement of your slime, setting it apart from generic desktop pets:    When you play music, your slime reacts in perfect sync with the rhythm, beats, and mood of the track, popping out playful musical note effects right on cue. Every unique melody becomes a lively, eye-catching animation on your desktop, elevating your music listening experience to a whole new level.    The game features a full built-in music player and management system, with support for track favoriting, playback history lookup, and album sorting. Curate your perfect playlists, and let your slime keep you company as you lose yourself in your favorite songs.    An optional, toggleable rhythm minigame is included. When you need a break from your day, dive into a casual rhythm challenge with your slime and your favorite tracks — one click to switch to laid-back fun, and melt away all your stress and boredom.    🎁 Steam Workshop + Friend Social Features: Unlock Endless Musical Fun  We’ve built full support for the Steam Workshop, and fully integrated Steam’s friend social system, so the joy of music doesn’t stop on your desktop — it can be shared with every fellow music lover:    Upload and share your curated music packs and playlists to the Steam Workshop, bringing your favorite tracks to players around the world.    Browse and download high-quality music content shared by other players at any time, with endless genres and playlists to choose from, so your slime always has fresh new beats to groove to.    Your audio creations, Workshop uploads, and in-game activity can all be synced directly to your  Steam Friend Activity . Let your friends see your latest creations the second you share them, and enjoy the fun of music and interaction together.    🎮 More Than a Desktop Pet — Your All-Day Cozy Companion  No mandatory quests, no complicated controls, no steep learning curve. Open the game, and instantly embrace non-stop heartwarming fun:    Left-click and drag your slime to move it anywhere on your screen — your entire desktop is your slime’s playground.    Left-clicking + mouse wheel can zoom in and out of slime.    The fully hand-drawn, adorable art style fits perfectly with any desktop aesthetic, adding a unique, cute touch to even the most plain work setup.    Full support for  Steam Family Sharing , so you can share this delightful little desktop joy with your friends with just one click.    ⚙️ Thoughtful, All-Scene Customization For Your Perfect Experience  We’ve refined every single feature and detail to fit seamlessly into every way you use your PC — non-intrusive, flexible, and totally tailored to you:    Handy preset keyboard shortcuts: F1 to reset your slime’s position, F2 to reset your slime’s size — never worry about your slime wandering off-screen again.    Full desktop environment support: Multi-monitor quick switching, one-click always-on-top window, and persistent system tray icon, so your slime can stay by your side quietly while you work, binge shows, or play other games.    Full personalization controls: Support for horizontal flipping of your slime, toggle between 5 built-in color schemes, and independent on/off switch for the rhythm minigame. Tweak every feature to match exactly how you want to use it.

about: Zhiqiu is a Windows desktop companion centered on English and Japanese vocabulary study. She stays on the desktop and responds while you learn, review, or take a break. Pet interaction, care activities, and mini-games are companion features built around a consistent study routine rather than replacements for it.    Core study features    • Two built-in default collections: English Study and JLPT Japanese Study, plus imports for your own decks and cards.  • FSRS scheduling for new cards and due reviews, with visible daily new-card, review, and overall progress.  • Choose a collection, stage, or individual deck as the active scope and continue from the previous session.  • Study meanings, examples, and pronunciation; rate memory strength and create a target-date study plan.    A customizable desktop companion    • Replace character artwork, motion states, interaction lines, and bound audio to create your own cute desktop pet.  • Share and subscribe to manifest-validated character content through Steam Workshop.  • Petting, dragging, care activities, music, and mini-games provide lightweight breaks between study sessions.    Base-game voice and AI content  The base game plays pre-recorded voice lines and does not generate text or speech using generative AI during gameplay. Mini-game recap text is assembled from authored lines according to game events. Some character images, animation variants, and fixed voice recordings were created with AI tools during development and are included as pre-generated assets.  Real-time AI voice generation is not included in the base game. It requires separately installed voice-runtime and voice-model DLCs.  Steam Workshop and user content  Steam Workshop supports sharing and subscribing to user-created character appearances, interaction lines, and local voice models. Uploaders must have the rights needed to share their content and follow Steam Community and Workshop rules. Inappropriate items can be reported through their Steam Workshop pages.  Workshop extensions require separate installation, activation, and configuration. The base game's vocabulary study, desktop interactions, and scripted mini-games do not require them.    The game supports Windows 64-bit only.

about: Dejinochi is a tiny virtual pet that lives on your desktop.  Hatch an egg, feed your pet, play minigames, clean up after them, and give them medicine when they're sick. They'll keep you company while you work, study, or do whatever else you're doing on your computer.  Every Dejinochi grows up differently depending on how you look after them. You'll have a record of them in your album, and sometimes they might even come back to visit. Then you can hatch another egg and start all over again.  As you play, you'll discover new species, unlock shells, collect stickers, and gradually fill up your album.  Dejinochi is meant to fit around your day. Your pet will get on with their own little life while you're busy, so you can check in whenever you have a moment.  FEATURES   Raise a virtual pet  Hatch an egg and take care of your Dejinochi as they grow. Keep them fed, play with them, clean up their mess, and look after them when they're feeling poorly.   Discover different species  The way you care for your pet influences what they grow into. Experiment with different routines to discover them all.   Watch them grow up and move out  Every Dejinochi eventually leaves home. Keep track of the pets you've raised in your album, and look out for familiar faces coming back to visit.   Customise your shell  Unlock different shells and decorate them with collectible stickers. Arrange them however you like.   Play minigames  Take a break with your pet and play a few little games together.   Create and install mods  Add custom species, shells, and stickers, or change how the game works. Dejinochi has been designed with modding in mind from the beginning.   Complete your collection  Discover every species, collect stickers, and keep a record of all the pets you've raised.   Keep a little pet on your desktop  Dejinochi runs alongside whatever else you're doing. Check in for a few minutes, then get back to your day.

A desktop virtual pet that slowly turns to horror.Estimated playtime: 4–5 hours.    Raise a Digima, a digital pet that lives on your PC, and dig into the secrets buried inside it. name: Keyarium
lang: English*, French*, Italian*, German*, Spanish - Spain*, Japanese*, Simplified Chinese*, Traditional Chinese*, Arabic*, Korean**
short: The ants create an empire in the corner of the desktop. Every keystroke is a rain of sweet nectar. Left untended, they build their kingdom, sometimes capturing an insect as a surprise. The scent of food from friends drives them in droves toward exotic flavors.
about: Keyarium is a quiet desktop ant‑ecosystem game that keeps you company on Windows. Ants live on your desktop, automatically foraging, nibbling, carrying, hatching, and fighting. You just work, study, or browse the web as usual – your keyboard activity is converted into energy, which you can use to drop food, grow your colony, and gradually build your own miniature ecological world.   Detailed Introduction   Place a small ant nest in a corner of your desktop and watch it run by itself.  Keyarium runs as a transparent, always‑on‑top, mouse‑through desktop window. It never asks you to stare at the screen or interrupts your daily workflow. Keyboard input is converted into energy, and energy lets you drop different kinds of food; ants will find the food, divide the carrying work, return to the nest, and bring resources to the whole colony.  As the colony grows, you can hatch more ants, unlock different castes like workers, soldiers, and males, and upgrade attributes such as speed, bite force, carrying capacity, lifespan, defense, and hatching efficiency. Different foods offer various nutritional combinations, and some may even attract insects to your desktop. Ants need to fend off insect attacks; after battles, the corpses can be turned into new food and rare materials.  If your Steam friends are also playing, when you drop high‑tier food there is a chance to invite your friends’ ants to cross‑screen foraging. Friend ants will appear on your desktop as an independent expedition team, and they will bring back resources after completing their tasks; you can also send your own ants to help your friends. The whole cross‑screen process works through Steam friends and P2P connections. When Steam is not running, the offline ecosystem still functions normally.  The game has no fixed level timers or mandatory daily quests. You can let your colony grow slowly in the background, or open the menu at any time to check resources, upgrades, the encyclopaedia, achievements, and friend status. Each time you return to your desktop, you will see new changes left by the ecosystem.   Key Features      Desktop companion gameplay : transparent, always‑on‑top, mouse‑through – the nest stays quietly in a corner of your desktop.     Automated ant ecosystem : foraging, nibbling, carrying, returning to nest, hatching, and life cycles flow naturally.     Keyboard‑driven energy system : use your computer normally to accumulate energy – no extra grinding needed.     Multiple foods and nutrition choices : from bread and cookies to salmon slices, each food has different costs, portions, and nutrient mixes.     Ant castes and growth : workers, soldiers, and males have different roles and abilities.     Upgrades and long‑term development : upgrade the nest, ants, and food to change colony size, efficiency, survival, and feeding strategy.     Insects and combat : flies, caterpillars, crickets, ladybugs, wasps, spiders, mantises, etc., can affect your desktop ecosystem.     Corpse resource recycling : insect corpses after battle can serve as food and provide rare materials.     Steam friend cross‑screen expeditions : invite friends’ ants to forage, or send your own ants to support friends.     Steam achievements and stats : achievement progress and unlock states sync with Steam, with offline‑play catch‑up support.     Achievements and encyclopaedia : record colony milestones, food collection, battles, and long‑term growth.     Multi‑language support : includes English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Italian, Spanish, and Arabic.     Optional input statistics : only counts key press events – does not read, save, or upload any specific characters, text, passwords, or window content; players can turn this feature off at any time. name: Idle Frontier
lang: Simplified Chinese, English, Traditional Chinese
short: An offline idle survival game for the gaps in your day. Keep its resizable window beside your work, start gathering and check back between tasks. Tend camps, craft, farm and explore at your own pace. Supplies still need care; pause whenever you need a break.
about: A Little Frontier Beside Your Work Welcome to Idle Frontier, an offline single-player idle survival and resource-management game told through text and a simple interface. Prepare food and water, start gathering, then get on with something else. The activity progresses on a timer without constant clicking or watching. Check back between tasks to collect the results, make supplies and decide what comes next. Make a Little Room for Your Camp Manually resize and position the game window in a corner of your desktop or beside your other work, and glance over at your resources and progress when it suits you. The game uses a conventional resizable window, not a transparent desktop pet or an automatically docked overlay.  When you have more time, tend your camps, chat with villagers or prepare for an active exploration trip. Hunger, thirst, storage and events that need confirmation still require occasional attention; this is not a fully unattended automation game. Need to concentrate? Pause whenever you like—the frontier can wait.  Start with a clearing in a fictional medieval world and gradually make it somewhere you look forward to returning. A brief visit can be a chance to prepare a little more for your next journey. Start with Some Firewood and a Warm Meal Set up gathering tasks, collect materials and craft dependable tools. Pack food and clean water before heading out, and keep an eye on hunger, thirst and your supplies. Cooking, pickling and drying help you make the most of what you've gathered. Your skills grow through use, making everyday preparations a little easier. Make a Camp Feel Like Home Choose a spot, build a camp, light a fire and add facilities that turn raw materials into useful supplies. Grow crops, look for better seeds and care for livestock. Establish camps in different places to give yourself a resting point on longer journeys. Watching a little planning turn into a good harvest is its own kind of adventure. Stop by the Village and Make New Friends Take a break from your chores and have a chat. Help residents with their requests, barter for what you need and get to know the people behind the familiar faces. A conversation or a helping hand can make an unfamiliar village feel a little more welcoming. Follow Your Curiosity Travel across a regional map generated from your world seed, notice the surroundings and wildlife, and prepare before choosing your next path. Your encyclopedia fills with things you've encountered, while new finds open up new possibilities. The surprises along the way? Those are yours to discover. Find a Pace That Suits You Play offline with saves stored on your own computer. Adjust the game speed and difficulty to suit you, enjoy making plans, or slow down to tend your camp and read your travel notes. I hope the frontier becomes somewhere you look forward to spending a little time. Come Play—and Help Me Make It Even More Fun! Thank you for taking a look at Idle Frontier! I'm continuing to improve the game, and I'd love to hear how it feels to play. Whether it's something you enjoyed, a clumsy interaction, a bug or a little idea you'd like to share, please get in touch through the Steam discussions. Your stories from the frontier are welcome, too.  I'm excited to hear from you and keep making this world more enjoyable together. Have a wonderful journey, and I'll see you by the campfire!

about: What is Bodyscope?   Bodyscope is not merely a game; however, it offers an interactive experience akin to one. It serves as a professional tool suitable for use by both experts and novices, facilitating the visualization of CT and MRI images in Virtual Reality. Each CT or MRI study comprises numerous 2D scans, which are utilized to construct 3D models in Virtual Reality. The complexity of the construction process increases with the number of scans in the study. The purpose of Bodyscope is to:  Generate realistic 3D models from real MRI and CT/PET images in VR, enabling easy comprehension of radiology data even without advanced spatial vision. Enhance understanding of MRI or CT/PET by allowing users to take an active role in learning through interaction with 3D models of real studies, rather than solely exploring cross-sectional or rendered images. With Bodyscope, users can:   Scale models to explore specific body parts in detail;   Apply a set of presets, distinct for CT and MRI images, to visualize specific tissues by density;   Cut pieces of VR models with special tools;   Take measurements of any element;   Enable additional lighting features to highlight elements of the interest;   Slice the model at any angle to remove interfering structures.   Collaborate with friends or colleagues Bodyscope has evolved beyond a technology generating hyper-realistic 3D patient data from CTs and MRIs enhancing situational awareness and spatial orientation for medical students and professionals. It now offers a collaborative environment! In collaboration mode, you can interact with your friends, colleagues, or even your physician and view the same VR model together. How it works Step 1: Run the converter  It's a simple and intuitive desktop app.  Step 2: Upload DICOM files  Anonymize your MRI, CT/PET study data if needed.  Step 3: View 3D models in VR  Rotate, slice, and adjust contrast for better visualization.  Step 4: Share your experience   Invite other learners to explore 3D models with you in virtual classes if you wish.

name: Slacking Squad
lang: English, Simplified Chinese
short: Slacker Squad is a lightweight desktop idle game that reacts to your keyboard and mouse activity. Work hard and your squad speeds up; slack off and they do too. Mine, cook, unlock characters, and capture defeated monsters as pets while your squad keeps you company.
about: Slacker Squad is a lightweight desktop idle game made to keep you company while you work.  When you start slacking off in real life, your squad members slow down too. But once you start hammering away at the keyboard and flinging your mouse around, they can feel the effort—   Time to go full speed!   You Slack Off, They Slack Off  The game dynamically calculates your squad’s work efficiency based on your keyboard and mouse activity.  When you work hard, they work hard.  When you start slacking, they immediately get the message.  The game only tracks keyboard and mouse activity frequency. It does not record what you type or click.  Tired of Working? Go Play Some Slacking-Off Minigames  Take a break from work and see what your squad brought back today.   Scratch-and-Reveal Wood Appraisal   Grab a scraper and slowly peel back the surface of a piece of wood.  Is it ordinary timber, or an extremely rare find?  You won’t know until you scrape it open.   Smash-and-Reveal Ore Appraisal   Grab a small pickaxe and start hammering away.  A plain-looking rock might be hiding a rare gemstone inside.  Work may not always come with surprises.  Rocks do.  I Can Rest. You Can’t.  Squad members lose stamina while working.  Running low?  No problem. You can roast some meat for them yourself.  Finished eating?   Good. Back to work.   That’s the whole idea:   You do the labor. I watch you do the labor.   Unlock More Slacker Squad Members  There are multiple characters to unlock.  Different squad members will work, slack off, gather resources, and react in their own way to whatever ridiculous orders the boss throws at them.  Can’t Beat Them? Bring Them Home.  Your squad may run into all kinds of monsters while out working.  Defeat them and you’ll have a chance to capture them as pets, letting them follow your squad members around.  Collect more pets over time and turn your small group of workers into an increasingly strange little workplace crew.  You Work, They Work  You don’t need to stare at the game all day.  Leave it running on your desktop.  Write code, make spreadsheets, argue with your boss—do whatever you normally do.  Then glance down every now and then.  Maybe someone is working at full speed.  Maybe someone has already started slacking off with the boss.   You work, they work.    You slack off, they slack off.

about: About Desk Tail        Desk Tail is a digital companion that lives on your Windows desktop. A ragdoll cat appears alongside your everyday work, watching your cursor, responding when you pet it, and settling down when things grow quiet.       There are no levels to grind, experience points to collect, or login streaks to maintain. Desk Tail focuses on a small number of polished interactions and the feeling that a familiar companion shares your desktop.  It Notices Your Cursor       Move the cursor and Desk Tail looks toward it. The response follows the cursor direction instead of playing a single fixed clip, creating the feeling that the cat has noticed what you are doing.  Natural Interaction and Rest  Give It a Gentle Pat       Click the cat’s head to receive a warm, restrained response. Afterward, it remains content for a short while before returning to its usual routine.  Quiet Idle Behavior       Desk Tail does not perform constantly. It may blink, look around, pause, or make a small adjustment, keeping the desktop calm rather than busy.  Settling Down to Sleep       After a quiet period, the cat can lie down, fall asleep, remain asleep, and wake again when you return.  Names and Shared Memories       You can name the cat and optionally tell it how you would like to be addressed. Both can be changed or cleared later. Desk Tail keeps local records of your first meeting, days spent together, selected interactions, and keepsakes without turning the relationship into visible statistics.       This is a lightweight local memory system, not an online AI that analyses your life or conversations.  Today’s Fortune and Two Personalities       Open Today’s Fortune for a small daily message. The result remains stable for the day and changes naturally on the next day. Choosing a zodiac sign is optional and only adds a light content preference; it is not professional astrology or a prediction guarantee.       Choose between a warm personality and a playful roast personality. Roasts are written as friendly teasing about habits such as procrastination, not as personal attacks.  Keep Me Company While I Work       Desk Tail includes a small set of work-companion tools. They are designed to make the cat part of your routine, not to turn the app into a full productivity suite.       Start a 25-minute or 45-minute focus session and end it at any time.       Take a 5-minute break, end it directly, or enable automatic breaks.       Enable or disable hydration reminders with 30, 60, or 90-minute intervals.       Create a local custom reminder.       Write a small note for today.  Weather and Keepsakes  Optional Weather       Select a supported city manually to view current weather. Weather requests require an internet connection and are sent directly to QWeather. Desk Tail does not read GPS location or use IP-based city detection.  Desk Tail Keepsakes       Save a local image containing the cat, its name, the date, and a short line of text. Keepsakes remain on your computer and can also be exported to a location you choose.  Local First       Desk Tail does not require a separate account. Names, preferred forms of address, relationship records, daily fortunes, reminders, notes, and keepsakes are primarily stored on your computer. Core companionship does not depend on a Desk Tail server. Weather and Steam platform features use their respective online services. Steam Cloud is not supported at launch.
